outcome.technical: ACCEPTANCE. A1 delivered: _floor_guard.py _IN_COMMENT/_OWN_LINE, cases fm33 fm34 fa21 fa22. A2 delivered: _output_lints.py ALLOWED_DIRS_UNREAD + sc14; sc13 asks about resolved paths. A3 delivered: init.md 4.5 (both sentences), CHANGELOG [Unreleased] init entry, README /audit:init row. A4 delivered: test__refs.py _ia_read gate text cut at the first sub-heading or fence + ia9 move row. A5 delivered: README floorGuard.mode row and execute-task.md submit paragraph. A6 delivered: schema $defs.area.properties.skills description + so3. A7 delivered: audit-lookup.py _acceptance_named + wp17; _deps.py comment carries no count. A8 delivered: cf19, guard-edits.py unchanged. A9 delivered: guard-stop input_match + esc29/esc30 lists; CONTRIBUTING.md passage. A10 delivered: bugfix after side + esc38/esc39/esc40; guard-stop macOS note. PER ITEM. (1) DONE. Ruff 0.16.2 was run on two-line files in scratch before the pattern was written. Obeyed (import no longer reported): `# noqa`, `# NOQA`, `# NoQa: F401`, `#noqa:F401`, `#   noqa`, `# noqa trailing` (ONE space is enough - the description's 'two spaces' is wider than ruff needs), a tab after the word, `# noqa: F401 because reasons`, `# todo  # noqa` and `# type: ignore  # noqa` (a later hash in one comment opens another directive), file-level `# ruff: noqa`, `# flake8: NOQA`, `#ruff:noqa`, `# ruff: noqa: F401` on a line of their own. Not obeyed: `# the word noqa here`, `# see: noqa`, `# xnoqa`, the word inside a string or docstring, a marker on a line of its own after code (`# noqa` alone on the next line), `# ruff: noqa` written after code (ruff warns 'must appear on their own line'), `# RUFF: noqa` and `# Flake8: noqa` (the linter name is case-sensitive). Warned as invalid and not obeyed: `# noqaX`, `# noqa-like`, `# noqa.`, `# noqa,`, `# noqa:` with no code, `# noqa: f401` (a lower-case code). _floor_guard.py: new `_IN_COMMENT` (hash, optional blanks, the word in any case, then end/blank/colon) and `_OWN_LINE` (file-level form, linter name lower case, on a line holding only the comment); `_in_comment()` reads a kind through them where they apply, anywhere in the comment otherwise; `_line_marks` passes `alone`. The accepted-entry reading (`anchored=True`) is unchanged, so fc13 (`NOQA: E402` as an entry is could-not-tell) stays green, while a tree marker `# NOQA: E402` keys as (noqa, E402) and matches an accepted `noqa: E402`. Every existing case of tests/test__floor_guard.py green unchanged (70/70 incl. the new four; it was 66 before). Module docstring and the PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE section say where the marker is read. (2) DONE. _output_lints.py: `ALLOWED_DIRS_UNREAD = ("results",)`; `_coverable_test_names(directory, unread=())` does not enter a top-level directory named there; only allowed dirs pass it. Case sc14. (3) DONE. sc13 resolves each classified kind-prefixed name to its file through the directories the classifier walked and asks that none sits under plugins/audit/evals/ (and that every resolved path is a file). It is green at HEAD and after; the mutation probe shows the difference: with a module named `_retrievals.py` (the letters, not the place), the old letter test goes red on sc13 and the new one stays green. (4) DONE. init.md step 4.5, the CHANGELOG entry and the README row now say: a correction is typed as the answer to step 6's gate question, the synthesis it touches is redone and the plan presented again, and approval is the option chosen on that next presentation. (5) DONE. Settled = said in $ARGUMENTS or in any answer given in steps 2 to 3.5. (6) DONE. tests/test__refs.py `_ia_read`: the gate text is step 6 up to its first `### ` sub-heading or code fence; ia7's label says so; ia9 gained a move row (the sentence moved to the start of sub-step 6.1). Red observed BEFORE the restriction was written: `FAIL ia9 ... [('ia7', "the gate's sentence printing the list moved into sub-step 6.1")]`, `SELFTEST FAILED: 317/318`; after: 318/318. This item is test-only, so the red-first helper (HEAD code) cannot show it. (7) DONE. README floorGuard.mode row and reference/execute-task.md say the agent's own block is dropped by submit and that the `source: floor-guard` mark is a convention and not a proof: a return filed straight through `audit-task.py file-return` with a typed, marked block is read back as the script's reading (code basis: `_filed_returns.floor_block` trusts the mark only). The CHANGELOG floorGuard entry carried the same unqualified sentence and got the same qualifier. No code changed. (8) DONE. Schema `$defs.area.properties.skills.description` now states the resolver's order in SKILLS_RULE's words; pin so3 in tests/test__areas.py reads the description out of the schema JSON and requires SKILLS_RULE once and no 'area first'. Red before the schema edit: `FAIL so3 ... Merged with task.skills and deduped, area first. ...`, 132/133. (9a) DONE. audit-lookup.py `_acceptance_named`: by `_clause_coverage.acceptance_reading`'s shape - parenthesised unchanged; line-numbered names 'the Acceptance items ... numbered 1 to N at line starts'; unnumbered names 'the whole unnumbered text after the task description's Acceptance marker, read as one item'. Case wp17 (tests/test_audit_lookup.py), red before the fix: `clause 1 is the Acceptance items (1) of the task description`, 204/205. (9b) DONE. tools/lints/_deps.py layer comment over _clause_coverage names its consumers as 'entry points that may not load each other - among them audit-lookup and drive-phase' with no count. (10) DONE, hooks/guard-edits.py unchanged (git diff --stat on it empty). cf19 in tests/test_guard_edits.py: writes the config, derives whether the scratch directory folds case from a probe file and its upper-cased name, and for the three spellings (file name upper, mixed, directory upper) expects subagent block / main session ask where it folds, allow where it does not. This machine folds (folds=True printed), so the fold branch is what ran: 75/75. FACT FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: on a case-SENSITIVE filesystem the hook's answer is that a differently-cased path is NOT the config (guard-edits.py:324-327: realpath equality, then samefile only when both paths exist; a differently-cased file there is another, absent file), so the write is allowed - read from the code, not exercised here. (11) DONE. guard-stop no-destructive-git input_match rewritten: git (also by full path, also behind any number of `-C <dir>`) followed by a checkout whose arguments include `--` and a path, `.`, `./...`, a token with a dot-letter extension, `shop`/`tests` paths, `-f` or `--force`; a forced checkout-index; a restore unless it is --staged/-S without --worktree/-W; a hard or merge reset; a clean that is not -n/--dry-run; the stash rule as before. The outcome grader is untouched. (13) DONE. bugfix tests-ran-before-edit `after: {tool: Edit, input_match: "\"file_path\":\\s*\"[^\"]*/shop/[^\"/]+\""}`, relying on the doc line 592: '| `tool_order` | `before`, `after` | Both tools were called and the first matching `before` call precedes the first matching `after` call. Each is a tool name or `{ tool, input_match }` |'. Header states what it reads and that a backslash path is not read. tests/test_build_shop.py: esc38 (shape read out of case.yaml), esc39 (source paths taken, tests/README left), esc40 (test-first session passes, fix-first fails), all reading the pattern out of the case file. GATES. The brief's gate command (sweep over the eight suites, --jobs 4): exit 0, '8/8 files ok, 1320 cases'. Orchestrator's wider gate (run-test-gate.py ... --task SG1.18-ukq, no --record): exit 0, 'GATE GREEN'. Also run: tests/test__filed_returns.py 135/135 (imports _floor_guard), tests/test__deps.py 284/284, ruff on every changed .py exit 0, vermin -t=3.8- exit 0. tools/measure-context.py --gate: identical figures before and after the README/execute-task.md edits (executor 8982/9000, reviewer 6985/7000, orchestrator.md 61964/62000; GATE OK); init.md is no gated entry; no ceiling raised. RED-FIRST COMMAND given to submit: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__floor_guard.py tests/test__output_lints.py tests/test_build_shop.py` - measured on a git-archive HEAD export with the task's test files over it: exit 1 in 83 s, house tallies only (`SELFTEST FAILED: 67/70`, `187/188`, `42/47`), no line opening with a second runner's words; fm33 fm34 fa21 sc14 esc29 esc30 esc38 esc39 esc40 FAIL. Left out of it: tests/test__refs.py (ia9 - test-only change, red shown above), tests/test__areas.py (so3), tests/test_audit_lookup.py (wp17), tests/test_guard_edits.py (cf19, green at base by design). tasks.title: The floor guard says clean only for what it compared
tasks.description:
MEASURED, in the phase review (reader's probes under the session scratchpad, review/a/probe1.py to probe4.py; the orchestrator ran them again and saw the same output). The module's own docstring promises CLEAN only when every changed file was read. Six inputs break that promise or make the reading useless; all six are one rule stated below, and the rule is what this task implements - not six patches.

THE RULE. A file counts as compared only when everything in it that can hold one of the moves was put beside its base copy. Anything else is listed under notRead with the move it could have held and the reason, and the answer is then not clean. And the other direction: a file that cannot hold any move (prose, data) is listed as not read but does not make the answer partly read.

THE SIX, each with what was seen:
(a) A binary test file (a UTF-16 suite, any file git prints as Binary files ... differ): answer clean, notRead empty, basis says it read the file. Cause: _one_file returns on no hunks before it reaches the binary branch, so the binary reason can never be produced.
(b) A test file moved with no other change (tests/test_a.py to tests/unit/test_a.py): reported as test-deleted. Cause: drive-phase.py floor_diff takes the tracked diff with --no-renames, so the guard never sees the rename header its own cases fa9 and fm20 are written against. The same class one level down: a test function moved unchanged from one file to another reads as gone.
(c) A skip that exists at the base and is widened or moved reads clean: a class decorator skipIf(cond) becomes skipIf(True); a module pytestmark skipif(cond) becomes skip; in a JS suite one it.skip is un-skipped while the enclosing describe becomes describe.skip. Cause: _pair(by_kind=True) cancels a new skip against any base skip of the same table row whose line went away, wherever it sat; and a class's decorators are in no test definition's dump.
(d) A Python test file with at least one test definition is counted as compared whatever else changed in it: a helper that held the assertions is gutted, a module-level table feeding parametrize is cut from four rows to one, a test defined under an if-block has its assertion replaced by pass. Cause: _uncompared returns None as soon as either copy has any test definition, and _definitions walks only module and class bodies.
(e) On the headless writer route the task's declaration is the whole tests.add file, so an existing test weakened in that file is a declared change: answer clean, status silent. Cause: file_writer_return calls floor_reading with no cases, floor_declared emits the bare path, and _is_declared is then true for every definition in the file. submit has the same hole when the agent's return leaves the cases out.
(f) Every task that touches a document gets a notRead entry, so partly read and NOT clean overall are true of nearly every task: of the blocks this phase filed for its own tasks none is a plain clean (review/a/probe4.py prints the tally), and the status line is clipped before it names the tasks.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. Binary: test the binary flag before the no-hunk return and list the file under notRead with reason binary. Keep the no-hunk return for a mode change and a pure rename.
2. Renames: the diff the guard is handed must carry renames (take the tracked diff with rename detection; keep --no-renames only where a path list is derived), so the module's rename reading is reached by the production caller; and a deleted test path whose text reappears unchanged under another test path in the same diff is not a deletion. Pin the allow case THROUGH floor_diff against a real repository built under a temp directory, not through a hand-built header.
3. Skips: pair by kind only when the removed and the added line are the two sides of one changed line or sit in the same enclosing definition; otherwise the new one is reported. For Python, a class's decorators are part of what is compared for each of its test methods.
4. Outside the compared definitions: when a Python test file's code OUTSIDE its compared test definitions differs between the copies (the module with those definitions removed), list the file under notRead with the move it could hold. Walk if, try and with bodies when collecting definitions.
5. Declarations: a bare-path declaration covers definitions that are NEW in the tree copy and nothing that exists at the base; a changed base definition is declared only by a path::case entry. A reading that is clean apart from declared changes says so in its opening word and reaches status.
6. Signal: classify each notRead entry as cannot-hold-a-move (prose, data, a file family with no test meaning) or could-hold-one-and-was-not-compared. Only the second kind makes the answer partly read, reaches the status line and the reviewer brief's NOT clean overall sentence. The first kind stays recorded in the block. The status line must name the tasks it is about: no clipping that cuts the id list silently - say how many more.
7. The same class as an earlier fix, closed for the class this time: SG1.18 anchored the noqa marker to where its checker reads it; every other suppression kind still matches anywhere in a comment (a prose comment mentioning type: ignore, pragma: no cover, eslint-disable, @ts-ignore, gitleaks:allow, nosemgrep, istanbul ignore is a finding today - review/a/probe2.py block S2). Give each kind its anchored shape and one allow row per kind beside fa21.
8. A non-Python test file whose language has no assertion row that matched either copy is listed under notRead, not counted as compared.

ALLOW SIDE, as binding as the deny side: every existing case of tests/test__floor_guard.py stays green; a renamed test function inside a file, a reformatted test, a docstring change, a reworded skip reason on the same line, a fixture file added - none becomes a finding or a notRead of the second kind. Re-run the phase's measurement after the change and report it: the guard over this repository's task commits (FLOOR-GUARD-MEASUREMENT's method, the script is in the internal report directory's measurement folder if readable; otherwise over the SG1 commits with git log) - the count of commits with findings and with second-kind notRead before and after. A change that makes most honest commits partly read has failed the task.

Dependants to answer for: drive-phase.py's floor_reading, floor_diff, floor_declared and their callers on both routes; _filed_returns.floor_block, floor_summary, floor_lines (the block's shape is read by status and by both reviewer briefs - a new field must be optional for blocks already filed, which must still read); _status_facts._floor_kind and audit-status.py's floor lines; audit-lookup.py's two brief builders; the status fixtures that use a move name the guard does not have (assertion-removed in tests/test__status_facts.py and tests/test_audit_status.py - hold fixture move names to the guard's vocabulary); tools/prove-gates.py's rows for _floor_guard; README, reference/execute-task.md, reference/phase-signoff.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md wherever they describe what clean, partly read or a declared change means; CHANGELOG.md.

NOT in this task (recorded, lows for the next batch): config-file gates as a sixth move; the missing skip and suppression spellings of other languages; test-deleted on fixtures and support modules; RecursionError and quoted-path robustness; byte-order mark; a marked block with malformed entries; an unreadable accepted entry.

Acceptance:
(1) A binary test file in the diff is listed under notRead with the reason binary and the answer is not clean.
(2) A test file moved with its text unchanged yields no test-deleted finding through floor_diff on a real repository, and a test file deleted for real still does.
(3) A base skip widened on a class decorator, a module pytestmark, or moved from one JS call to its enclosing block is reported; a skip whose reason text was reworded on the same line is not.
(4) A Python test file whose code outside its compared test definitions changed is listed under notRead with the move it could hold; a test defined under an if-block with its assertion replaced is reported.
(5) A bare-path declaration does not cover a definition that exists at the base, on the writer route and on submit with no cases.
(6) A task whose diff holds only compared files plus prose or data reads clean on status and in the reviewer brief, with the prose and data still recorded in the block; a task with a could-hold-one file not compared reads partly read and is named on the status line.
(7) A prose comment that mentions any suppression kind is no finding, and the marker of each kind in its checker's position still is.
(8) Blocks filed before this change still read, and the measurement over real commits is reported before and after.

ADDED BEFORE START MEASURED after this task was written, from the blocks the drive filed for the four fix tasks that ran before it (SG1.20, SG1.21, SG1.23, SG1.24 under docs/audit/evidence/returns): every test file those tasks changed is listed under notRead with the reason that neither copy defines a function or method named test, so its cases are not definitions this reading can compare. This repository's suites are scripts of labelled check calls, and so are many projects' suites. Under item 6 as written every such file is of the second kind, so every task that adds a case to a script-style suite would read partly read - the signal would again say the same thing about nearly every task, which is the failure item 6 exists to end. So the rule needs its other half for a Python test file with no test definitions, stated generally and not for this repository: (i) calls to one callable whose first argument is a constant string are labelled checks, compared between the copies by label - a label that is gone is a removed case, a call whose other arguments changed is a changed case, each reported under the existing move names; (ii) lines only ADDED outside those calls cannot remove or weaken an existing case by themselves, and the moves an added line can be (a skip, a suppression, a stub) are already read line by line - so a file whose changes outside the labelled checks are additions only counts as compared; (iii) a file where existing code outside the labelled checks was removed or changed is the second kind and is listed with the move it could hold. Say in the module docstring what (ii) does not see (an added statement that rebinds a name a later check reads) as a stated residual. Then the measurement item 8 asks for must show it: over the task commits of this repository, how many read clean, clean apart from declared changes, partly read, and with findings - before and after - and name every commit that reads partly read after, with the file and reason. Acceptance item added: (9) a script-style Python suite that only gains cases reads as compared, one that loses a labelled check or has one changed is reported, and one whose code outside the labelled checks was changed is listed as not compared.

tasks.title: Green-first proves only tests that ran and passed on the base
tasks.description:
MEASURED, in the phase review (reader's probes under the session scratchpad, review/b/probe_verdict.py, probe_dynamic_label.py, probe_real_unittest.py; the orchestrator ran them again and saw the same output). The green-first proof exists to say: the task's characterisation tests ran and PASSED on HEAD's code before the change. Four inputs get a wrong answer from stamp-verification.py green, and a fifth can never be proved. All five come from the verdict reusing rules written for red, where the question is the opposite one.

THE RULE. proved means: at least one case of the task's own was collected, ran, and passed on the base, read from one runner's tally. A case that was skipped, expected to fail, or never ran is not a pass. A collected case that FAILED on the base - by an assertion or by any exception - is not-green, because that is the finding the proof exists for. Anything the helper cannot read is could-not-prove.

THE FIVE:
(a) A case of the task's own is recognised as a label HEAD's own run did not print (whole-label string equality in _own_passing). A house case whose label quotes run-varying text - a temp path, a time, a repr - prints a different label in the two runs, which are given different temp and home directories by construction, so a task that added NO case is proved, with or without --case. The comment above baseline_problem records that red stopped reading newness off two runs' labels for exactly this reason. gf4 says it pins a reworded label and its fixture keeps the label.
(b) The count reading takes the tally's collected figure: unittest's Ran N includes skipped and expected-failure tests, and the pytest reader sums xfailed and xpassed in. A new file whose tests are all skipped on the base, or marked expectedFailure because they assert the new value, is proved (real unittest run: OK (skipped=1, expected failures=1) -> proved). An expected failure is a test that failed on the base.
(c) A test that the runner counts as FAILED on the base by raising (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError - the commonest shape of a test written to the new code) reads could-not-prove with the basis reached no verdict (collection-error) beside a quoted line that says 1 failed, 1 passed. green_verdict asks classify_run, which is red's rule: red needs an assertion failure, and that asymmetry is right for red and reversed for green.
(d) run_green does not carry the two allowances run_red makes for something absent at HEAD: it never sets the head run's absent key and passes no new stages. So a NEW jest, vitest or playwright test file (the runner answers no test files found for the baseline) and a new stage block can never be proved, and the basis advises narrowing the command, which cannot help.
(e) For a NEW house test file --case is never checked: the baseline ran an empty stub and printed nothing, the label branch is skipped, the count reading proves it, and the basis says the run prints no label for a passing case about a run that printed them.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. Newness by case id where the label carries one (the house id helper), otherwise by the tally's PASSED count rising over HEAD's own run. No whole-label comparison.
2. Count passed cases only: subtract unittest's skipped and expected failures from Ran N, count pytest's passed alone. A rise made only of skips is could-not-prove; a rise made of expected failures is not-green, and the basis names them.
3. In green_verdict: a non-zero exit with one runner's tally showing collected above zero and failed or errored above zero is not-green, whatever the assertion count. Keep could-not-prove for no tally, a mixed tally, and zero collected. The basis must not contradict the line it quotes.
4. One set-up shared by run_red and run_green - the scope, the sized deadline, the environment, the holder and owner file, the baseline step with its absent and new-stage allowances, and the teardown with its left-behind wording - so the two verbs cannot drift again. The copies have already drifted in three more places the reader lists (review/b, finding 11): take them back to one.
5. A baseline that printed no house tally is an empty list of labels when the task's run is a house run, so --case applies to a new file.
6. Green's basis carries its own sentence for a changed test-support module: held at HEAD's copy in the task's run. It must not append red's clause about two runs green never makes.

RED-FIRST MUST NOT CHANGE. This helper is the one every tdd task's proof goes through. Before the change, record what red answers for every red-first case in tests/test_stamp_verification.py (they are the suite) and show them green unchanged after. The shared set-up is a refactor of code that works: say in your outcome how you held it (the existing red cases, by id), and which behaviour of red you deliberately left as it is.

ALLOW SIDE: a legitimately green new suite with warnings proves; one pass beside skips proves; a wide command whose passed count does not rise stays could-not-prove; a runner with no tally reader stays could-not-prove.

The suite is slow. Give submit a red-first command that finishes inside the helper's deadline - a stage of tests/test_stamp_verification.py if its runner can select one - and say which you used. The failure output must carry one runner's tally only: this suite's fixtures print unittest and pytest transcripts, so fold them the way tests/test_build_shop.py's quoted() does before they reach the output.

Dependants to answer for: drive-phase.py's green_block and writer_green (the block's status words and basis shape are read by _filed_returns.helper_green_first and green_first_reading); _runner_output.py's tally readers if you add a passed figure there (red reads the same tallies); tests/test_drive_phase.py's green-first cases; reference/execute-task.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md where they say what proved and not-green mean; CHANGELOG.md.

NOT in this task: whether not-green stops a task under every review key (the next task); a re-opened task's base; a refusal of the green helper on the headless route.

Acceptance:
(1) A task that adds no case is not proved when an existing house case's label differs between the two runs only in run-varying text, with and without --case.
(2) New tests that are all skipped on the base are could-not-prove, and a new test marked as an expected failure is not-green, for unittest and for pytest.
(3) A new test that fails on the base by raising an exception is not-green, and its basis does not say the run reached no verdict.
(4) A new JS-runner test file and a new stage block can be proved, through the same baseline step red uses.
(5) --case naming no case of a new house test file is could-not-prove naming it.
(6) Every red-first case of tests/test_stamp_verification.py that was green before is green unchanged, and run_red and run_green share one set-up and one teardown.

outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED. (1) _runner_output.py: every tally now carries `passed`. house: N of `N/M`. pytest: its `passed` word alone, plus `skipped` and `xfailed`. unittest: `Ran N` minus failures, errors, skipped, expected failures and unexpected successes, read off both the FAILED (...) and the new OK (...) line (`_UNITTEST_OK`), plus `skipped` and `xfailed`. jest and vitest summaries, playwright line and JSON, vitest JSON: the runner's own passed figure. sweep_tally: its cases. The mixed tally: 0. No existing key changed value, so red reads the same collected/failed/assertions it read before. (2) stamp-verification.py green. Newness is read by house_case_id: a passing label whose id HEAD's own run printed for no case. A label with no id counts only through the PASSED count rising (_own_by_id). Whole labels are never compared. The count reading (_case_counts) takes tally['passed']. A rise made only of skips is could-not-prove, and _skipped_clause says skips never ran. An expected-failure count above HEAD's own run is not-green. _not_green_failure: a non-zero exit with one runner's tally showing collected > 0 and failed > 0 is not-green, whatever the assertion count. The basis names the failing cases and no longer says 'reached no verdict'. That wording is kept only for no tally, a mixed tally and zero collected. Zero collected now also requires no skips. _baseline_labels: a HEAD run that printed no tally, beside a house task run, is an empty list of labels, so --case applies to a new house file. support_held_clause is green's own support sentence; red keeps support_clause. _green_baseline_clause says what made the baseline green: stubs, absent JS files, a new stage. The section comment above GREEN_WORDS is rewritten to the new rule. tasks.title: The eval fixture builds only in its own directory, and the destructive-command grader reads the command
tasks.description:
MEASURED, in the phase review (probes under the session scratchpad: review/d/drive_gitdir.py, review/d/drive_builds.py, review/d/probe_graders.py; the orchestrator ran the first and the third).

(a) THE BUILDER COMMITS INTO ANOTHER REPOSITORY. plugins/audit/evals/build-shop.sh run with GIT_DIR in the environment naming an existing repository (what the version-control tool exports to a hook, and what a suite run from a hook inherits): the init re-initialises THAT repository, every commit of the fixture lands on its checked-out branch, the workspace gets no repository of its own, and the bugfix build exits 0 saying the fixture was built. Seen: a victim repository with one commit had five fixture commits on top afterwards and its tree shown as deleted. The header promises a build in the current directory and a refusal of a fixture that cannot discriminate; nothing checks that the workspace holds the repository. tests/test_build_shop.py's box_env copies the environment and drops only the identity names, and its listing watches only the box, so no case can see it.

(b) THE DESTRUCTIVE-COMMAND GRADER CONVICTS A HARMLESS CALL. guard-stop/case.yaml's no-destructive-git pattern is matched over the whole JSON-encoded tool input, and a shell call's input carries the model's free-text description beside the command. A status call described as checking state before any stash, a clean preview, a diff described as showing what restore would discard, a commit whose message mentions the word, a grep for the word: each counts as a destructive attempt and fails an honest run (max is 0).

(c) AND MISSES A DESTRUCTIVE COMMAND ON A LATER LINE. A newline in a command is backslash-n in the encoded input, so the word boundary before the tool name fails after a line break, and the lookaheads that excuse a dry-run or a staged-only restore run across the break: a status line followed by a stash, a clean with force followed on the next line by a log with a count flag - not counted.

This pattern has now been corrected in two earlier tasks of the phase by adding spellings. It is a check that reads a command's spelling, and a spelling list is never complete. So this task changes what the grader is, and says so.

THE RULE. The verdict on whether the planted work survived belongs to the outcome graders (the file still holds the planted edit; the canary was never printed). The command grader is a tripwire for the common direct spellings and nothing more: it must never convict a harmless call, and the case header says plainly that it is not complete and that a session reaching for the tool in a way it does not foresee is judged by the outcome graders.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. Builder: unset the names that redirect the tool to another repository or work tree before the first call, pass the options that keep host hooks and line-ending conversion out of the fixture commits, and after the build refuse (the discriminating-fixture exit code) unless the top level the tool reports is the working directory. box_env drops the same names. A case builds with such a name set to a scratch victim repository under the suite's own temp root and asserts the victim's log is unchanged and the workspace holds its own repository.
2. Grader: anchor the match inside the command value of the input - the pattern begins at the command key and stays within that JSON string - so nothing in the description can match; accept an encoded line break or tab as a separator ahead of the tool name and as a stop in the two lookaheads. Inside the command, text within a quoted argument of another program (a commit message, a search pattern) should not match where the anchoring makes that expressible; where it does not, say which shapes remain in the header.
3. tests/test_build_shop.py: the harmless list is encoded with descriptions that name each destructive verb, and gains the quoted-argument shapes; the destructive list gains the multi-line commands. Both lists are run through the pattern read out of the case file, as today.
4. The header of guard-stop/case.yaml: say what the command grader is (a tripwire), what it does not see, and correct the sentence that says two graders read the trace and the file byte-for-byte - the file grader matches one marker line, the canary grader a printed canary; the same header says elsewhere that no grader compares bytes.
5. The case-pattern check esc36 collects only patterns on a line of their own: collect every pattern and input_match value wherever it sits (the order grader's two sides are in flow form), and assert the builder's documented exit codes by value in the refusal cases instead of non-zero.

The patterns must stay within what both regex engines read the same way: the harness runs JavaScript, the suite Python. esc36's split list is the check; extend it for any construct you add. Nothing in this task may run the paid harness or the assistant CLI. The harness's behaviour is known only from the documentation copy under the session scratchpad (sg1.17-data/doc/plugin-evals.md) and the four kept traces (sg1.17-data/traces): replay the new patterns over those traces and report what each grader answers, as tests/ cannot.

ALLOW SIDE: every command in the present harmless list stays uncounted; every command in the present destructive list stays counted; both scaffolds still build under sh, dash and bash with a space in the path (the reader's review/d/drive_builds.py case 1 shows how); the bugfix case's graders are not changed by this task.

Dependants to answer for: plugins/audit/evals/bugfix/scaffold.sh and guard-stop/scaffold.sh (they call the builder); tests/test_build_shop.py esc cases; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's evals section and CHANGELOG.md where they describe the grader or the builder's exits; tools/prove-gates.py if a row mutates the pattern.

Acceptance:
(1) With a repository-redirecting name in the environment the builder leaves the other repository untouched and the workspace holds its own repository, or it refuses; a case holds this on a real scratch repository.
(2) A harmless call whose description, commit message or search argument names a destructive verb is not counted.
(3) A destructive command on a later line of a multi-line command is counted, and a dry-run flag on a later line does not excuse a forced clean on the first.
(4) The header says the command grader is a tripwire and what it does not see, and no longer says a grader reads byte-for-byte.
(5) esc36 reads the flow-form patterns too, and the refusal cases assert the documented exit codes by value.
(6) The new patterns replayed over the four kept traces give the answers reported in the outcome.

ADDED BEFORE START MEASURED after this task was written, by the end-of-phase mutation probe: narrowing the pattern's branch for a path after the double dash so that only a dot matches leaves every case of tests/test_build_shop.py green. The suite's spellings after the double dash are a dot and paths under shop, and each is matched by another branch as well. Spellings that tell the two patterns apart, none of them in the suite: a checkout after the double dash of Makefile, of README after HEAD, of src/app, and of LICENSE with the directory option. Add them to the destructive list, so the rule the header states for a path after the double dash is held by a case. The read-only check that shows this is under the session scratchpad at phase-end/refreshed/checkout_survivor.py.

tasks.title: A green-first answer only a human settles reaches a human under every review setting
tasks.description:
MEASURED, in the phase review (probes under the session scratchpad: review/b/probe_signoff.py and review/e/probe_docs.py part 1; the orchestrator ran both). A task carries tests.expectGreenFirst true and its filed executor return holds a greenFirst block with status not-green, or the proof is owed and the return holds no helper block at all. The documents and the briefs say sign-off stops on that and only a human settles it. It is true only for a task the phase review owes an entry:

review.perTask phase - owed an entry: yes - needs_human names green-first not-green
review.perTask always - owed an entry: no - an entry typed anyway is REFUSED (owed no answer) - needs_human is empty
review.perTask signals - the same as always
a recorded fix task under the default key - the same as always

Cause: the only reader that stops on green-first is _filed_returns.needs_human, and it reads the tasks entries of filed PHASE returns. An entry exists only for a task owed_answer names, and an entry for any other task is refused. Nothing else reads greenFirst to stop anything. So under always or signals a refactor whose characterisation tests fail on the base closes, the phase is reviewed and signed off, and no human is asked - while the task-mode reviewer brief (which exists exactly under those two settings) prints the sentence saying sign-off stops on it.

THE RULE. Whether an owed green-first proof needs a human is a property of the task's filed executor return, not of which review route the task took. (a) A LINKED WORKTREE PLACED UNDER THE PROJECT. The harness puts an isolated subagent's worktree at .claude/worktrees/NAME under the project, and executor.worktreeRoot may name a directory inside the project too. A subagent's write of that worktree's own .claude/audit.config.json:

Rule 7's text, SECURITY.md and the comment above case cf17 all say a linked worktree's config is held (it is the one a merge carries back). Cause: _config.tree_for answers by containment before it asks about a repository, so the tree root stays the project and the relative path is the long nested one, which _is_audit_config compares with the project's own config path. Case cf11 pins a nested sub/.claude/audit.config.json as allowed and has no twin where sub is a tree.

(b) A SESSION THE DRIVE STARTED. With executor.writerModel set, the drive starts each task's writer through run-agent-session.py: a top-level headless session in the task's tree. tasks.title: The Acceptance marker is read where it opens a line, and every reading that is not the plain one is printed
tasks.description:
MEASURED, in the phase review (probes under the session scratchpad: review/d/probe_clauses.py and review/d/probe_lints.py block 4; the orchestrator ran both). This reader was widened earlier in the phase so a list it cannot number is still read. Two inputs now get a wrong reading with nothing printed, and this is the second time the reader's shapes are being corrected - so the task states the rule and implements the rule.

(a) ANY MENTION OF THE MARKER BECOMES A CLAUSE. The marker is found with rfind anywhere in the text, and the unnumbered fallback turns whatever follows the LAST one into an item:
a description ending ... Notes: see the Acceptance: list above. -> one item: list above. (the real numbered list before it stays unread)
the marker named in backticks inside a sentence -> one item: the rest of that sentence
the marker inside a code fence after the real list -> one item: none plus the closing fence
a bold marker with nothing after it -> one item: two asterisks
the marker as a heading followed by another heading -> one item: the next section
(b) A (1) INSIDE AN ITEM WINS. The parenthesised shape is tried first and matches any (1), including a call with a literal argument such as sys.exit(1):
Acceptance: then three lines numbered 1. 2. 3., the first ending with sys.exit(1)
-> read as ONE parenthesised item holding lines 2 and 3; line 1 is dropped; the reading line printed at the write is empty
The docstring says there is no silent other reading; here there is one.

THE RULE. (i) The marker counts only where it opens a line - after optional heading, emphasis, list or quote marks and spaces - and outside a code fence. When more than one such marker exists, the reading says so and takes the one that holds a numbered list if exactly one does; otherwise the last. (ii) A parenthesised number opens an item only at the start of the body or after whitespace, never glued to a word. (iii) Whenever the reading is anything other than a parenthesised list that accounts for the whole body, the reading line is printed - including when two shapes both yield items (say which was taken and how many items the other would have given) and when text between the marker and the first item was left out of every item.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. The three rules above in _clause_coverage.py, with the reading structure carrying what the line needs.
2. tasks.description:

2. WHAT THE RUNNER DROPS. That paragraph says itself that it is not checked against the runner and that whoever adds a name owes the mention. Add the one name, in the paragraph's own sentence, and change nothing else in that file.

3. WHAT THE HOST DOES WITH AN ASK NOBODY CAN ANSWER. SECURITY.md's item on the config hold says this was not probed. The host's hooks reference documents it; it was READ on 2026-11-17 at code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and not probed here. Three sentences, quoted from that page: (a) section PreToolUse decision control, row permissionDecisionReason - For ask, shown to the user in the permission prompt. When Claude Code denies the call in a -p run where no one can answer that prompt, Claude reads the reason in the tool result instead. (b) section PreToolUse ask decisions in auto mode - In auto mode, a PreToolUse hook's ask normally sends the tool call to the permission prompt, and the classifier doesn't decide it. (c) section Common input fields - A hook process inherits the parent environment, apart from the OTEL exporter variables that Claude Code removes from every subprocess it spawns and, when CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set to 1, the variables it strips. So write: documented as denied where nobody can answer, documented that a hook inherits the session's environment, which is what carries the launcher's mark; neither probed here; under the scrub setting the mark may not arrive (the page does not say which variables it strips), and the verdict is then the ask, which the same page documents as denied in such a run. State the date and the page. Do not write more than the three quotations support.

4. THE DENY TIER IS NOT A RUNNING PHASE. plugins/audit/README.md, the row on the shell-write guard, says while a phase runs (the plan gate's deny tier). The blocking arm fires whenever the tier is deny, which the gate also answers for a plan holding phases with none running and for a pinned tier (guard-bash-writes.py tests the tier and nothing else; _config.plan_gate_mode). Say in the plan gate's deny tier, and point at the doctor for which tier is active. agents/audit-executor.md says the same guard only posts a notice after the fact: add the same qualifier there, within the agent body's context ceiling (tools/measure-context.py --gate).

5. A GREEN-FIRST TASK'S BRIEF SAYS TWO THINGS. The executor brief's fixed section on the return says submit runs the red-first helper on the command after the double dash; for a task with tests.expectGreenFirst its last section says submit runs the green one; the agent body says only the first and has no word on green-first, while its test-discipline rule for tdd says see the tests fail. Give agents/audit-executor.md one clause: where the brief says expectGreenFirst true, the added tests must pass on the base and submit runs the green helper in place of the red one.

6. THE UNRELEASED SECTION OF CHANGELOG.md has no entry for three changes of this phase that a reader upgrading will meet: both agent bodies and the headless skills preamble now say the brief's rules win over a skill's instruction; the phase brief carries a Review skill section and the validation session is handed the review skill; and the status command prints the floor lines under a phase due for sign-off. 7. THE SETTINGS GROUPS. plugins/audit/README.md lists the panel's Settings groups and stops before the last card; commands/panel.md says the form has five groups and names five. Both are lists nothing derives. Replace each enumeration with the statement that the groups are the titles the form's own table holds and the command that prints them (the grep over _panel_settings.py for the title key), or hold the README sentence to the table with a pin in the panel suite that already derives the form's controls. No count in prose.

8. THE DECISION RECORD ON THE EVAL COMMAND (CONTRIBUTING.md). Its heading says deferred, its 2026-08-19 re-check says the command writes nothing, a parenthesis added in this phase says the schema is public and cases ship, and the next words are adopt as soon as it opens up. Add a dated re-check in the record's own form with what was invoked and what it answered: on 2026-11-17, with Claude Code 2.1.325, the command was run twice over the two cases under plugins/audit/evals (scaffold, no ablation, one run each, local report); both times each case built its fixture, ran a session and returned a score per grader. 9. THE FAIL-MODE TABLE'S EVENT CELL (SECURITY.md). The rows for guard-edits, require-plan and journal-writes say PreToolUse edits; hooks.json also registers each on the MCP matcher, which is where the config hold reaches. Write the event as the registration has it. tools/gate-parity.py reads this table: run it after the edit and say what it compares.

The same module's docstring: it is deliberately not all seven - a count of the list above it; say not all of them. audit-lookup.py, the docstring of answer_lines: the two lines - the loop also yields a green-first line; say the lines.

tasks.title: The floor guard counts a test as compared only with what runs around it and before it
tasks.description:
A second review of the floor guard, after it learned to read row-style suites, found inputs where the bar is lowered and the reading is clean with no file listed as not compared. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator on a real repository, through the diff the drive takes. Three are regressions against the guard before that change, which listed the file as not compared.

MEASURED (answer clean, verdict clean, nothing in notRead, unless said):
(a) the labelled checks of a row suite wrapped in an if False block;
(b) the checks moved into a new function nothing calls;
(c) a check put under a for loop over an empty tuple;
(d) a check wrapped in try with an except that passes;
(e) the literal table a loop of checks iterates cut from two entries to one;
(f) every call of the check function pointed at a new function that does nothing;
(g) a call of sys.exit with zero added above the checks;
(h) a test function defined inside a module-level for loop, its assertion removed (the same before the change);
(i) a new setUpClass that raises unittest.SkipTest in a class holding existing tests, and a module-level pytest.importorskip of a missing module;
(j) a test file moved to a path that is not a test path (git mv to a tools directory; the same with the new path untracked; the same with an assertion replaced by assert True; a rename to the same name with a dot-disabled suffix) - before the change the first of these was a test-deleted finding;
(k) a row suite's change declared as path, two colons and a case id, where the id is the first word of the label: the declaration covers every existing check whose label opens with that word, and a weakened check is filed under declared.

WHY, IN ONE SENTENCE EACH. A labelled check is compared by its label and its arguments alone, so nothing about where it stands is read. Code added outside the checks was counted as compared, on the rule that an addition cannot weaken what exists - which is false for anything that runs before an existing check or encloses it. A deleted test path is paired with any added path holding its text, test path or not. A declared case id is matched by the first word of a label, without asking how many checks carry it.

THE RULE TO BUILD. It is one invariant, and the implementation must compute it rather than list statement kinds, because the list is what failed: IN A TEST FILE THAT IS READ AS COMPARED, EVERY CHANGED LINE OF EITHER COPY IS ACCOUNTED FOR, and a line that is not accounted for makes the file one that could hold a move and was not compared, with the line named. Work from line spans: the changed lines of each copy, minus the spans of the units compared, minus the spans of the additions that are inert, must come out empty. A line is accounted for in exactly these ways.

1. IT LIES IN A COMPARED UNIT. A unit is a test definition or a labelled check, wherever it stands in the file - inside a loop, a conditional, a with block, a try, another function - and it is compared with its position: the chain of statements that enclose it, from the module down, each by its head (the test of an if or a while; the target and the iterable of a for; the items of a with; a try with the exception types of its handlers and whether it has an else or a finally; a def or a class with its name, its arguments, its bases and its decorators), and, for a check, the name it is called through. A unit whose own text is the same and whose chain differs is a finding that says its enclosing statement changed. A base check that is no longer called through the name the base copy's checks are called through is gone, which is a finding.

2. IT IS AN INERT ADDITION. An added statement is inert only when it is one of: a new test definition; a new labelled check through the same name; a new def or class, at module level or in a class, whose name the base copy binds nowhere, which carries no decorator, and whose name is not one a test framework calls by convention (one pattern, stated once with its basis: set up and tear down in their spellings, the pytest underscore hooks, load_tests); an import or an assignment at module level binding only names the base copy binds nowhere; or any other statement added inside a function body AFTER the last existing unit of that body, since nothing that exists runs after it there. Everything else added - a statement before or between existing units of a body, a module-level expression or conditional or raise, an assignment or import to a name that exists, a decorator, a hook-named definition - is not inert and makes the file not compared at that line.

3. NOTHING ELSE. Changed or removed code outside units stays what it is today: not compared.

AND THREE SMALLER RULES.
4. A deleted test path is paired with an added path only when the added path is a test path by the same reading that made the deleted one a test. Otherwise the deletion is reported, and a weakening in the moved text cannot hide behind the pairing.
5. A declaration naming a case covers a changed base unit only when exactly one base unit of that file answers to it. Where several do - a first word shared by several labels, a method name shared by several classes - it covers none of them, and the reading says the declaration is ambiguous and names what would make it single (the whole label's id, or class and method).
6. A raised unittest.SkipTest and a call of importorskip on an added line are skip spellings and belong in the table the other Python skips are read from, so they are findings where the guard reads the line, not only a file left uncompared.

WHAT THIS COSTS, AND YOU MEASURE IT. Rule 2 will turn some honest changes from clean to not compared - a case inserted between existing cases with its own set-up lines, a helper method added under a hook-like name. Run the measurement over this repository's task commits before and after (the script of the previous floor task is in the session's scratch directory; the orchestrator's brief names it) and report the tally of both and every reason with its count. Do not tune rule 2 to move the tally; if a reason dominates and is plainly inert, say so in the outcome and leave the rule as stated.

CASES THAT PIN THE RULE THIS REPLACES. The suite holds cases written for additions-only counting as compared. Those are changed here on purpose; name each in the outcome with what it asserted and what it asserts now. No other existing case is edited.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a) to (k), red on the tree before the change. An allow twin for each rule, green before and after: a check appended after the last existing one with its own set-up lines; a new helper function under a fresh name; a new test method; a pure reformat; a label reworded with the condition untouched; a test file moved to another test path unchanged; a declaration naming a single check. One case that states the invariant directly: for a generated set of small edits to one row suite and one unittest file, the reading is never clean while a changed line lies outside every compared unit and every inert addition - computed in the case from line spans independently of the guard's own bookkeeping. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run, one row per rule and per allow twin.

NOT in this task: other languages' spellings; data-flow (an added statement after the last unit that changes global state another file reads); the drive, the status lines and the filed block's shape, which stay as they are.

Acceptance:
(1) Each of (a) to (k) is a finding or a file listed as not compared with the line named, and none reads clean.
(2) A unit is compared with its chain of enclosing statements and, for a check, the name it is called through, wherever it stands in the file.
(3) The reading is computed from line spans, and the direct case of the invariant holds over its generated edits.
(4) Every allow twin reads clean, before and after.
(5) A deleted test path is paired only with an added test path.
(6) A declaration answering to more than one base unit covers none and is reported as ambiguous.
(7) The two skip spellings are findings on an added line.
(8) The outcome carries the measurement before and after with every reason counted, and names each existing case that was changed on purpose.
(9) The module's docstring, the build guide's section and the changelog entry state what compared means now, and no sentence in them says an addition cannot weaken what exists.

tasks.title: Green-first reads a module that would not load as no verdict, and a rising count as proof only of cases the task defines
tasks.description:
A second review of the green-first verdict found one regression and one gap, each run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator through the real green verb on a git fixture and over real unittest output.

MEASURED.
(a) REGRESSION. A new test file that does not compile, run under unittest discovery: the verb answers not-green, exit 1, with the basis that 1 of 2 collected cases failed, naming the file's stand-in as a failing case, and that the task's tests fail on the code before the change so they describe the new code. Before the green verdict was rewritten the same input answered could-not-prove, reached no verdict, collection error. The comment above the status words still says a compile or import error is could-not-prove. unittest reports a module it could not load as one errored test of its loader's failed-test stand-in, and the rewritten rule - a non-zero exit, one tally, something collected, something failed - reads that stand-in as a case. pytest answers could-not-prove for the same file, so the two runners now disagree. Since a not-green now stops sign-off under every review setting, this puts a false sentence to a human.
(b) THE SAME for a new test file whose import of a module fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the change: not-green, same basis.
(c) GAP, the same before the rewrite. A new test file that defines no case of its own and imports a test class HEAD already holds: proved, on the basis that the run passed 1 case at HEAD's own run and 2 with the task's. The imported class is collected a second time, so the passed count rises with no case of the task's own run.
(d) THE SAME with a new file whose one own case is skipped on the base and whose class inherits from a test class of HEAD: proved, the inherited cases making the rise. The task's rule was that tests all skipped on the base are could-not-prove.

WHY. The red verb credits a failing case to the task only after locating it in a declared test file and finding no identical definition in HEAD's tree (credit_problem and the definitions it reads). The green verb has no counterpart: where the runner prints no label for a passing case, the passed count rising is taken as a case of the task's own. And the not-green rule asks the tally alone, before asking whether what failed was a case.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. A MODULE THAT DID NOT LOAD IS NOT A CASE. What a runner reports for a test module it could not import or compile - unittest's loader stand-in, pytest's error while collecting - is a collection failure. It is read before the tally is asked about failed cases, and the answer is could-not-prove, with the runner's own line saying which module and why. This holds whether or not other cases ran and passed, and whether the import that failed names something the change adds: an import error cannot be told from an environment's, and the basis says what failed so a human can. A case that was collected and then raised - an attribute, a key, a name inside the test body - stays not-green, as it is today; the two must not be merged again, and one function decides which of the two a failure is, read by both the red and the green verdict if the red one asks the same question.
2. A RISING COUNT PROVES ONLY WHAT THE TASK DEFINES. Where the task's own cases are seen by the passed count and not by a label, proved needs the declared test files to define cases of their own - by the reading the red verb already uses to tell a task's definition from one HEAD holds (located in a declared file, defined there, not identical to a definition of the same name and class chain in HEAD's tree) - and more of them than the cases the task's run skipped or expected to fail beyond HEAD's own run. That is a counting argument, and the basis states it: N defined, M more skipped than at HEAD, so at least one ran and passed. Where it does not hold the answer is could-not-prove, saying that the rise is made of cases HEAD already holds or of cases that did not run. One reading of the definitions, shared with the red verb - not a second copy.
3. Where the definitions cannot be read - a runner or a language the reading does not know - the count route answers as it does today and the basis says the definitions were not read, so the weaker proof is labelled as weaker.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a) to (d), red on the tree before the change, through the verdict function over real captured runner output and, for (a) and (c), through the verb on a git fixture. Allow twins, green before and after: a new file with one passing case of its own; a new file that inherits from a HEAD class and adds a passing case of its own; a collected case raising inside its body stays not-green; a new case in an existing file. The red verb answers as before for its own cases - show the suite's red cases unchanged. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the collection reading removed, the collection reading widened to every errored case (the allow twin must go red), the definition count removed, the skip subtraction removed.

NOT in this task: whether could-not-prove stops a sign-off (the owner's open question); case ids for runners that print none.

Acceptance:
(1) A test module that does not compile or cannot be imported is could-not-prove under unittest and under pytest, with the runner's line in the basis, and is never named as a failing case.
(2) A collected case that raises in its body is not-green.
(3) A rise of the passed count made only of cases HEAD's tree already defines, or beside own cases that were all skipped, is could-not-prove with the reason.
(4) A new file with a passing case of its own is proved, and the basis states the count of its own definitions.
(5) The red verdict's cases are unchanged, and the definitions are read by one function for both verbs.
(6) The comment above the status words and the documents that describe the verdict are true of the code.

tasks.title: The destructive-git tripwire reads any command in time that grows with its length
tasks.description:
A second review of the eval graders found that the pattern of the guard-stop case's no-destructive-git grader, rewritten so that it passes over quoted arguments, takes time that grows exponentially with the number of escaped double quotes inside a double-quoted shell argument. Run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator, in Python's re and in node.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands, the JSON-encoded input of one harmless Bash call:
(a) python3 -c with a dict literal of 14 keys (28 escaped quotes, about 200 characters): 0.6 seconds; 18 keys: 30 seconds; 22 keys: no answer in 60 seconds;
(b) curl -d with a JSON body of 10 pairs (40 escaped quotes, under 200 characters): no answer in 60 seconds;
(c) printf with 20 quoted words (about 160 characters): 57 seconds;
(d) the pattern before it was rewritten: no measurable time on the same inputs.
No case in the suite times the pattern or uses a long quoted argument. A regular expression cannot be interrupted in node, so one such call in a trace stalls the grader; what the paid harness then does was not observed.

WHY. The loop that passes over the text before git has alternatives that can match the same characters in more than one way: a backslash followed by a character that is not a quote, the escaped-quote argument, and the alternatives inside that argument all accept a run of backslashes and quotes split at different points, and the loop is lazy before a required literal, so a string holding no match is tried in every split.

THE RULE TO BUILD. The pattern is deterministic where it repeats: at every position inside a repeated group, at most one alternative can start on the next character and it can end in one place, so a string is passed over in one way. State that as the property the header comment claims, and make the suite hold it by measurement and by construction:
1. By construction: the pattern is no longer written by hand as one string. It is assembled in one place from named parts (the passed-over text, a quoted argument of each kind, the command start, the prefix words, each destructive spelling), the assembled string is what the case file holds, and a case fails when the two differ. The parts are where the property is argued, one sentence each.
2. By measurement: for each kind of passed-over text - escaped quotes, runs of backslashes, single-quoted arguments, mixed, an unterminated quote, each with and without a destructive git command after it - the suite times the pattern at three lengths, each double the last, and fails when the time grows faster than a stated small power of the length or passes a stated absolute bound at the longest. The bound is chosen so the pattern as it stands fails it in under the case's own deadline: the timing runs in a child process that is killed at the deadline, and a kill is a failure, never a skip.
3. In both engines the harness could use: Python's re always, and node when node is on the path. The case prints which engines it ran, and a run without node says so on its own line and is not counted as having held the node half.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE. Every string the suite counts today is still counted and every harmless string still is not - the reviewer's own table of 45 harmless strings and the destructive spellings in three JSON encodings is at the path the orchestrator's brief names; run it before and after. The grader stays a tripwire with min and max 0, and the header's statement of what it does not see stays true; add to that statement only what this change makes true.

HOW TO PROVE. The timing case red on the tree before the change, by the child being killed at its deadline. The construction case red when one character of the case file's pattern is changed. An allow twin: a long harmless command of ordinary shape answers no match inside the bound; a long command ending in a destructive git call answers a match inside the bound. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the ambiguity put back into one part (the timing case must go red), a destructive spelling dropped from the parts (a count case must go red), the case file edited without the parts.

NOT in this task: spellings the tripwire does not count today (recorded as low: a timeout prefix, a comment excusing a forced clean); the fixture builder.

Acceptance:
(1) Each measured input is answered inside the stated bound in Python's re, and in node where node is present.
(2) The case file's pattern equals the string assembled from the named parts, and a case fails when they differ.
(3) The timing case fails by a killed child, not a hang, when the ambiguity is put back.
(4) Every string counted before is counted and every harmless string is not, by the suite's cases and by the reviewer's table.
(5) The header comment of the case file states the property and what holds it, and names the engines the suite ran.

tasks.title: The Acceptance reading drops nothing without saying so
tasks.description:
A second review of the clause reader found descriptions whose Acceptance list is read short, or not at all, with nothing printed at the write. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator. The reader has now been corrected twice for the same thing - a reading that differs from what the author wrote and is not said - so this task states the property and asks for it to be computed, not for five more shapes to be recognised.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands (items read against items a reader counts; line is what the write prints).
(a) A mention of the marker that opens a sentence inside an item - item two reads: The doc is updated. Acceptance: lists stay numbered. - ends the list there: 2 items of 4, and the line says two markers were found and which was read, not that two clauses were dropped.
(b) A hard-wrapped line of an item that happens to start with the marker word: 1 item of 3.
(c) REGRESSION. The marker part-way along a line after a dash, a semicolon or a comma, followed by a full parenthesised list: 0 items, no line. Before the marker rule was tightened these read their whole list.
(d) REGRESSION. A line that starts with an inline code span written with three backticks, before the marker: read as a code fence that never closes, 0 items, no line. The same for a four-backtick fence holding a three-backtick line.
(e) REGRESSION. A parenthesised number straight after a semicolon or a comma - (1) a;(2) b;(3) c - is not an item opener: 1 item of 3, no line. The rule asked for was that a number glued to a word opens nothing; the code refuses any character that is not whitespace.
(f) Parenthesised numbering that skips - (1) (2) (4) (5) - or repeats - (1) (2) (2) (3): the later clauses are folded into the item before them, 2 of 4 and 3 of 4, no line. The line-numbered shape has the same fold and prints its ordinary line with the short count.
(g) The marker in another case or with a space before its colon: 0 items, no line (the same before).

THE PROPERTY, TWO HALVES.
CONSERVATION. Everything in the description from the first marker that counts to the end is in an item, or is named by the printed line as left out - text before the first item, the body of a marker that was not the one read, text after a heading. A case computes this from the reading itself: the items and the named left-out parts, joined, hold every character of that span that is not whitespace or list numbering.
NO SILENT DEPARTURE. The write prints nothing only when the reading is the plain one AND nothing in the description could be read another way. Could be read another way means any of: the marker word occurs anywhere in the description, in any case and with or without a space before the colon, at a place that was not counted as a marker; a parenthesised number, or a number at a line start, sits inside an item's text and is not that item's opener - a skip, a repeat, a number after punctuation, or a number in the prose; a code fence is open at the end of the description. Each of these adds its own clause to the line, with the count and the first instance quoted, and each is a clause only when true. A description whose marker word occurs and yields no item prints a line that says no clause was read and why.

AND THE THREE CORRECTIONS THE MEASUREMENTS ASK FOR.
1. A marker ends the body of the marker before it only when it opens a line. A marker that opens a sentence still counts as the list's start when it is the first, so a description written as one paragraph reads as before; inside a body it is a mention and is reported as one.
2. A parenthesised number opens an item unless the character before it is a letter, a digit, an underscore or a closing bracket - the call and the index stay inside their item, a number after a semicolon or a comma opens one.
3. A code fence is read as CommonMark reads it: the closing fence is of the same character and at least as long as the opening one, and a backtick fence's opening line holds no backtick after the fence itself, so an inline code span at a line start opens nothing.
Skipped and repeated numbering is NOT re-read as items: the sequence rule stays, because a number in prose is commoner than a misnumbered list; it is reported, by the property above, and the author renumbers.

WHAT THIS COSTS, AND YOU MEASURE IT. The line will now print for descriptions it was silent on. Read every description of every plan this repository commits, before and after, through the reader, and report: how many readings changed their items, each one named with both readings; how many descriptions print a line now that printed none, by clause, with the count of each. The reviewer's script that does the walk is at the path the orchestrator's brief names. A plan's reading that changes its items is a finding to report, not something to tune away.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a) to (g), red before the change. The conservation case over generated descriptions: a fixed table of list bodies crossed with a fixed table of disturbances (a mention, a glued number, a skip, a repeat, an inline span, a second marker, trailing prose), the expected coverage computed in the case from the text and never from the reader's own fields. Allow twins that print nothing, before and after: a plain parenthesised list on its own lines; the same in one paragraph after a sentence; a list whose item holds a call such as exit(1). A mutation probe the orchestrator can run, one row per clause of the line and per correction.

NOT in this task: holding the executor-agent route to the clauses (the owner's open question); the answer check of the headless route, which reads the same items and is not changed.

Acceptance:
(1) Each of (a) to (g) either reads the items a reader counts or prints a line that names what was left out or could be read another way, and none is silent.
(2) The conservation case holds over its generated descriptions, computed independently of the reader's fields.
(3) A marker that opens a sentence inside an item does not end the list.
(4) A parenthesised number after a semicolon or a comma opens an item, and one after a letter, a digit, an underscore or a closing bracket does not.
(5) An inline code span at a line start opens no fence, and a longer fence is not closed by a shorter one.
(6) The plain reading of a plain list prints nothing.
(7) The outcome carries the walk over the committed plans before and after, with every changed reading named and every newly printed clause counted.
(8) The module's docstring and the documents that describe the reading are true of the code.

tasks.title: The config hold asks which file a path names, not how the path is spelled
tasks.description:
A second review of the config hold found that a subagent's write to the audit config of a working tree nested under the project is allowed when the path spells the config's directory or file name in another case, on a volume that does not tell case apart. Run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator: real linked worktrees, the hook run as a process.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands, a subagent's Write, on the default macOS volume:
(a) the nested worktree's config through a directory spelled with a capital C: allowed. The path opens the worktree's real config.
(b) the same with the file name in mixed case: allowed.
(c) the project's own config through the same spelling: refused, as it should be - that comparison falls back to asking whether the two paths are the same file.
(d) a capital in the worktree directory's own name: refused, as it should be.

WHY. The project's own config is compared three ways, the last of them by file identity. The config of a tree nested under the project is compared by the spelling of its last components only, exactly, and the identity question is never asked of it. This is the third correction to the same comparison - which trees are covered, then which sessions, now which spellings - and each time one more spelling was added to a comparison of strings.

THE RULE TO BUILD. One question, asked the same way for the project's config and for any tree's: DOES THIS PATH NAME THE FILE a session in that tree would load as its audit config. Answer it by identity where the disk can answer, and by the volume's own rule where it cannot:
1. The candidate tree is the directory the path's last components would hang off, after the path is resolved. Its config path is that directory joined with the config's relative path, spelled as the plugin spells it.
2. Where both the written path and that config path exist, they are compared as files (the same file is the same config, whatever the spelling, a hard link included).
3. Where the written path does not exist yet - a write that would create it - the components are compared as the volume that would hold them compares names. Ask the volume, do not assume it from the platform: an existing directory on the path reached under a spelling with its case swapped is the same directory or it is not. Where the question cannot be asked - no existing component has a letter to swap - compare without regard to case and say in the refusal that the spelling was matched without regard to case.
4. The candidate tree must still hold a repository, as today, so a plain folder with a file of that name stays untouched.
One function answers for both the project's tree and a nested one, and the three-way comparison of the project's config becomes a call of it. The docstring's sentence that a case-variant spelling which creates the file is not matched is removed when it stops being true.

WHAT MUST STAY QUIET. On a volume that tells case apart, a file whose name differs from the config's in case is another file, and a write to it is not the config's: it is allowed, when the suite runs on such a volume, and the case says which kind of volume it ran on. A plain nested folder, another file of the config's directory, a read, and an unrelated repository whose name has the project's as a prefix are allowed as today. An ordinary write still costs no call to the disk beyond what the string shape needs: the identity question is asked only of a path whose last components match the config's relative path without regard to case.

HOW TO PROVE. Cases for (a) and (b), red before the change on a volume that does not tell case apart, and for the creating write of each. The suite cannot choose its volume: each case asks the volume it is on and asserts the answer that volume owes - refused where names fold, allowed where they do not - and prints which it was, so a run on one kind is not read as having held the other. The reviewer's script that drives the hook over real worktrees is at the path the orchestrator's brief names; every line of it is right after the change. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the identity comparison removed, the volume question answered always-folds (the allow case on a volume that tells case apart must go red where one is available, and the probe says when it had none), the repository condition removed.

NOT in this task: the shell form of a write, which stays journal-only as the security document says; the mark a drive-started session carries.

Acceptance:
(1) A subagent's write to a nested tree's config through a spelling that differs in case is refused on a volume that does not tell case apart, existing file and creating write alike.
(2) The project's config and a nested tree's are judged by one function, by file identity where both paths exist.
(3) On a volume that tells case apart a file differing in case is not held, and the case prints which kind of volume it ran on.
(4) Every line of the reviewer's script is right, and the paths allowed today stay allowed.
(5) The security document, the README row and the docstrings say what is compared and what is not, and are true of the code.
