tasks.title: The floor guard calls a test file compared only when nothing but its tests changed
tasks.description:
A third review of the floor guard found, again, inputs where the bar is lowered and the reading is clean with nothing listed as not compared. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator on a real repository, through the diff the drive takes. This is the third round on the same class, and the cause this time is in the rule the last task was given: it listed kinds of ADDED code that count as harmless, and every kind on the list can run something.

MEASURED (answer clean, verdict clean, nothing in notRead):
(a) a statement clearing the list of failures, added after the last check and before the existing line that turns failures into the exit code - the rule called anything after the last check harmless because nothing that exists runs after it, which is false for the verdict line;
(b) the same statement appended to the body of the check function itself, which every check calls;
(c) a call ending the run, assigned to a fresh name above the call of main; the same call as the body of a new class; the same as the default of an argument of a new function - a new binding was called harmless by the name it binds, and what it evaluates was never read;
(d) an assignment to a fresh name whose value is a call replacing the check function, or replacing an assertion method of the test framework, by one that does nothing;
(e) a new method under a name the framework calls on every test without the suite naming it;
(f) a labelled check cut from one suite and placed in a new file of the same diff under a condition that is never true, or inside a function nothing calls - a check moved between files is matched by its label and arguments alone, while a moved test definition is matched with its enclosing statements;
(g) REGRESSION. An assertion in a helper moved from the body of an if into its else, or from the body of a try into its except handler: clean. Before the last task these were listed as not compared. Statements outside tests are matched as a flat sequence, and their place in the enclosing statement is not part of what is matched.
And (h): the case written to hold the invariant computes its expectation from a second copy of the same list of harmless additions, so it cannot go red for (a) to (e).

THE RULE TO BUILD. No list of harmless code. A Python test file of the diff is COMPARED only when both of these hold, and each is a comparison of syntax trees, not of lines:
S. THE REST IS THE SAME. Take every test unit out of each copy's syntax tree - a unit is a collected test definition or a labelled check statement, as the guard finds them today - and what is left of the two trees is identical: the same statements, in the same order, each in the same place of the same enclosing statement. Layout, comments and blank lines are not in the tree and so are never a difference.
U. EVERY EXISTING UNIT IS STILL THERE AND STILL THE SAME. Each unit of the base copy has one twin in the tree copy with the same own syntax, the same position - the chain of enclosing statements from the module down, each by its head and by WHICH part of it holds the unit (the body, the else, which handler, the finally), and the number of statements that are not units standing before it in that part - and, for a check, the same name it is called through.
A unit of the tree copy with no twin in the base is a NEW unit: counted, named, and not judged.

WHAT EACH OUTCOME IS CALLED.
- U fails for a unit: a finding, as today (changed, gone, or moved - the reading says which, and moved says from where to where), unless declared by case as today.
- S fails: the file could hold a move and was not compared, as today's kind for that. The reason says which of two things it is, computed and not guessed: ONLY ADDED - the statements left of the base copy all appear in the tree copy's, in order and in place, and the tree copy has more (the first added statement is named with its line); or CHANGED OR REMOVED - anything else (the first statement of the base copy with no place in the tree copy is named). An author reading the report must be able to tell a new helper from an edited one.
- S and U hold: compared. With nothing else found in the diff the reading is clean, and its basis says how many existing units were compared and how many are new.
A unit moved to another file of the diff is the same unit only with the same position there, the file apart; otherwise it is gone from the first file, which is a finding.

WHAT THE READING DOES NOT CLAIM, STATED IN THE MODULE AND IN THE DOCUMENTS. It compares structure and never evaluates code. A new test or a new check can itself do anything when it runs, and the reading says new, not harmless. Code outside the test files of the diff - a changed helper module, a conftest in another directory - is read by the other rules of the guard or not at all. These sentences replace the paragraph that lists what an addition cannot do.

WHAT GOES. The list of inert additions, the pattern of hook names, the matching of statements outside tests as a sequence, and the line arithmetic that subtracts spans: S and U replace them. If something of them must stay for a reason this description does not see, say which and why in the outcome.

WHAT THIS COSTS, AND YOU MEASURE IT. Every new helper, import or line of set-up outside a new unit now makes its file not compared, where the last rule let some through. Run the measurement over this repository's task commits before and after (the previous floor task's script and its tallies are where the orchestrator's brief says) and report: the tally of verdicts before and after; of the files not compared after, how many are ONLY ADDED and how many CHANGED OR REMOVED; and that no commit lost a finding it had. Do not tune S or U to move the tally.

CASES THAT PIN THE RULE THIS REPLACES are changed on purpose; name each in the outcome with what it asserted and what it asserts now. No other existing case is edited.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a) to (g), red before the change. The invariant case rewritten so that it cannot share the guard's blind spots: over a generated set of edits to a row suite and a unittest file - a fixed table of edit operators applied at every statement position, the operators including an inserted call, an inserted assignment whose value is a call, a new definition whose default is a call, a statement moved between the parts of an if and of a try, a unit moved under a new condition, a unit moved above the statement before it, a pure reformat, a new unit appended, a new unit inserted between two units - the case computes the expected outcome with its own small tree comparison written in the case, by a different route from the guard's (for example by unparsing each copy with its units deleted from the source text by their line spans, and comparing the two texts' dumps), and the guard must agree on every edit. Allow twins, clean before and after: a new check appended after the last; a new check inserted between two checks; a new test method; a pure reformat of a unit and of a helper; a label reworded with the condition untouched; two adjacent checks swapped; a test file moved to another test path unchanged. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run, one row per half of the rule and per allow twin.

NOT in this task: other languages; evaluating what added code does; the drive, the status lines and the filed block's shape, which stay as they are (a new reason TEXT inside the existing shape is not a new key).

Acceptance:
(1) Each of (a) to (g) is a finding or a file listed as not compared with the statement named, and none reads clean.
(2) A Python test file is compared only when its tree with the units taken out is identical in both copies and every base unit has a twin with the same syntax, position and, for a check, callee.
(3) The module holds no list of additions that count as harmless and no pattern of hook names.
(4) A file not compared says whether code outside its tests was only added or was changed or removed, and names the first such statement.
(5) A check moved between files is matched with its position, as a test definition is.
(6) The invariant case computes its expectation by its own tree comparison and agrees with the guard on every generated edit, and goes red when either half of the rule is removed from the guard.
(7) Every allow twin reads clean.
(8) The outcome carries the measurement before and after, the split of files not compared, and names each existing case changed on purpose.
(9) The module's docstring, the build guide's section, the README row and the changelog entry state the rule and what the reading does not claim, and no sentence in them says an addition is harmless.

INVARIANT ROUTE (fx4): units found by the case's own walk, their line spans overwritten in the source text by a placeholder name, the two texts' ast.dump compared with placeholders deleted; the kind by deleting the tree statements whose every line difflib calls inserted and comparing again; a unit's position by the dump with only that unit marked - no helper shared with the guard. tasks.title: Green-first proves by taking the task's own tests out, and a failing case outranks a module that did not load
tasks.description:
A third review of the green-first verdict found two regressions in the reading of a module that did not load and four inputs where proved is answered with no case of the task's own having run. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator through the real green verb on a git fixture. This is the third correction of how a case of the task's own is told from the rest, each of the earlier ones a rule read off the runner's printed text or off a count, so this task replaces the argument instead of adding to it.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
A MODULE THAT DID NOT LOAD.
(a) REGRESSION. One new test file does not compile and another new file's own case fails an assertion on the base: could-not-prove, the basis naming only the file that did not load. Before the last task: not-green. The load failure is read first and returns before a failing case is asked about.
(b) REGRESSION. An own case fails an assertion whose message quotes a line shaped like the loader's stand-in; or, in pytest's layout, a failing test whose captured output holds a line starting with the word the collection summary starts with: could-not-prove, could not load. Before: not-green. The reading matches any line of the whole output.
Both turn an answer that stops sign-off into one that stops nothing.
A RISING COUNT.
(c) A test method defined in a plain class the runner never collects, beside a subclass of a HEAD test class: proved, 1 defined.
(d) A subclass of a HEAD class adding a case that FAILS on the base, the command deselecting it by name: proved.
(e) The own case in a declared file the command's pattern does not run, a second new file re-running HEAD's class: proved.
(f) A class-level skip raised in setUpClass over two own cases: proved, 2 defined more than 1 more skipped - the runner counts a class-level skip once.
(g) An own case under a skip decorator bound to another name: proved by the weaker route, with 0 defined and 1 more skipped in the same basis.
(h) REGRESSION on the allow side. A passing case generated at import with setattr: could-not-prove, with the reason that the rise is made of a HEAD class the file imports or inherits - it imports none. Before: proved.

WHY. The proof counts what the declared files DEFINE and what the run SKIPPED, and argues that more defined than skipped means one ran. Whether a definition is collected, selected, run, or skipped under its class is not in either number, so each of (c) to (g) is a way for the two numbers to say yes while nothing of the task's ran.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. PROVED IS A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO RUNS OF THE SAME FILES. Where the task's own cases are not seen by a printed label, the baseline run - HEAD's own tests on HEAD's code - is made with each declared Python test file that is new at HEAD laid over NOT as an empty file but as itself with the task's own test definitions taken out: every test definition the red verb's reading calls the task's own (defined there, and not identical to a definition of the same name and class chain in HEAD's tree), removed from the source by its span, decorators included, a class or function left without a body given one that does nothing. Everything else of the file - its imports, its classes and their bases, its helpers, a test it copies from HEAD - stays. The task's run is as today. Then the passed count rising between those two runs is the task's own definitions running and passing, because nothing else differs between them: a definition never collected, deselected, not run by the command, skipped by its class, its module or a renamed decorator, adds nothing to the second run, and a HEAD class imported or inherited is in both. The basis states it that way: the two counts and the definitions taken out, by name. This is the green verb's baseline alone; the red verb's baseline stays the empty file it is today.
2. A declared test file that exists at HEAD keeps HEAD's copy as its baseline, as today: what the task added to it is already the difference.
3. NO OWN DEFINITION, NO PROOF BY COUNT. Where the declared files hold no definition the reading can take out - cases generated at import, built by a loader hook - the answer is could-not-prove, and the reason says exactly that: no test definition of the task's own was found to take out, and a case generated when the module loads is not one. The sentence about a HEAD class is printed only when a HEAD class is imported or inherited.
4. Where the file with its own definitions taken out does not load on the base, that is the baseline not being green: could-not-prove, the runner's line in the basis. This is the same answer rule 6 gives for the whole file, by the same reading.
5. Runners and languages whose definitions the reading cannot take out keep today's baseline and today's count route, labelled as the weaker proof in the basis as today; the label names the reason. State in the module which runners those are.
6. A FAILING CASE OUTRANKS A MODULE THAT DID NOT LOAD. The run is read in this order: a collected case of the task's run that failed or errored and is not a module's load failure makes the answer not-green, and any module that did not load is named beside it in the same basis; only when no such case is left does a module that did not load make it could-not-prove.
7. A MODULE THAT DID NOT LOAD IS READ FROM THE RUNNER'S OWN REPORT OF IT, not from any line that resembles one: under unittest, the errored entry whose id is the loader's stand-in AND whose block, between that header and the next entry or the summary rule, carries the loader's own sentence; under pytest, a path named in the collection-error section AND in the short summary as an error. A line inside another case's failure message or captured output is inside that case's block and is never a load failure. The red verdict reads the same function, and its basis no longer says could not load for a case that was collected.

WHAT THIS COSTS, SAID IN THE OUTCOME. A case of the task's own that OVERRIDES an inherited test of the same name runs in place of it, so taking it out leaves the count where it was: could-not-prove, where the truth is that one ran. A case generated at import is could-not-prove. Say both in the module and in the document, with the reason, as limits.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a) to (h) through the real green verb on a git fixture over real unittest runs, red before the change; pytest's layout through the verdict function over text in that layout, saying so. Allow twins, the same before and after: a new file with one passing case of its own; a subclass of a HEAD class adding one passing case; two own cases, one skipped and one passing; a new case added to a file HEAD holds; a collected case raising in its body, or in setUpClass, stays not-green; the house and sweep routes untouched, shown by their cases. The red verb's cases unchanged. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the baseline put back to an empty file (a case of (c) to (g) must go red); the removal widened to every definition in the file, HEAD's copies included (the copied-test case must go red); the order of rule 6 reversed; the block reading of rule 7 widened back to any line.

NOT in this task: whether could-not-prove stops a sign-off; jest and vitest beyond the label of rule 5; a runner option that prints one line per case.

Acceptance:
(1) Each of (c) to (g) is could-not-prove through the real verb, and the basis names the definitions taken out and the two counts.
(2) A new file with a passing case of its own is proved by the difference between the file with and without its own definitions.
(3) A run holding both a module that did not load and a failing collected case is not-green and names both.
(4) A line shaped like a load failure inside a case's failure message or captured output is not read as one, under unittest and in pytest's layout, by either verb.
(5) A file with no definition to take out is could-not-prove with a reason that is true of it.
(6) The allow twins answer as before, and the red verb's cases are unchanged.
(7) The module, the build guide, the changelog and the reference document state the rule and its two limits and are true of the code.

tasks.title: The Acceptance reading is silent only when a wider reading of the same text finds the same items
tasks.description:
A third review of the Acceptance reader found descriptions where the items differ from what the author plainly wrote and the write prints nothing. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator on the tree as it stands. The last task gave the reader a list of things that count as a departure - the marker word before a colon, a parenthesised number in an item - and each finding is a shape that list did not name. So this task does not add shapes to the list: it makes the silence a comparison of two readings.

MEASURED (items read, items a reader counts, line printed):
(a) a parenthesised list whose later items are numbered at the line start with a dot or a closing bracket - `(1) ..`, `(2) ..`, then `3. ..`, `4. ..`: 2 read, 4 written, nothing printed. One description in this repository's own plan does this: the fifth item silently takes a whole block added later that numbers its points at the line start;
(b) the marker written with emphasis around the word and the colon outside it, as a heading with no colon, followed by another word before the colon, followed by a dash, or with a no-break space before the colon: 0 read, 2 written, nothing printed. On the headless-writer route such a task is held to no clause;
(c) numbers in full-width brackets, or a character that has no width inside the marker word: read short, nothing printed;
(d) the reader's own check that no text after the marker is left outside every item and every named part can be replaced by one that always answers nothing, and the suite stays green: no case shows it can find anything;
(e) REGRESSION, on input nobody writes: forty thousand list numbers or marker mentions on ONE line take seconds and hold gigabytes, where before the last task they took a twentieth of a second - every one of them is given a copy of the rest of its line, and only the first is ever quoted.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. TWO READINGS OF THE SAME TEXT, BY THE SAME READER. The reader's choices - what spells the marker, what opens an item - become its parameters. The STRICT reading is today's and is what a task is held to; nothing about which items it reads changes in this task. The WIDE reading takes every choice at its widest:
   - the text is first folded to Unicode's compatibility form and its format characters dropped, so full-width brackets and digits, a no-break space and a character without width read as their plain twins. This is one normalisation, not a list of characters;
   - a marker is any line whose first word is the marker word in any case, once markup that can stand before or around a word is set aside (heading signs, emphasis, a quote sign, a bullet, backticks, blanks), whatever follows the word on that line; and the word followed by a colon anywhere, as today;
   - an item opens at a number in any of the forms the reader knows for either list style, and in a square bracket, at a line start after indentation and a bullet, and - for the parenthesised form - after a blank as today.
   State the wide reading's choices in ONE table in the module, each row a parameter and its strict and wide value; the wide reading is the reader called with the table's wide column, not a second parser.
2. SILENT ONLY ON AGREEMENT. The write prints nothing only when the strict reading is the plain one (as today) AND the wide reading finds the same items: the same count, each with the same text once both are folded the same way. Otherwise the line says so in the reader's existing form and adds how many items the wide reading finds and where the two first part: the line number and the text there.
3. WHAT PRINTS TODAY STILL PRINTS. Every description that gets a line today gets a line that says at least as much. Where a detector of today's (the marker mentions, the stray list numbers) is now answered by the comparison, it goes, and the outcome says which went; where one must stay, say which and why.
4. THE CONSERVATION CHECK IS PINNED. A case calls the check that looks for text outside every item and every named part with spans that leave a gap, built by the case, and it names the gap; and a second case shows that the reading's answer goes red when that check is made to answer nothing.
5. TIME AND MEMORY GROW WITH THE LENGTH. A quoted part is cut to a fixed number of characters where it is taken, not when it is printed, and no part holds the rest of its line. A case times the reading at doubling lengths over many list numbers on one line, many mentions on one line and many markers on one line, and holds the growth to about linear and the largest to a ceiling, in a child killed at a deadline.

WHAT STAYS QUIET. A plain description: one marker spelled as the plugin's own commands write it, at a line start, its items in one numbering style, no other line starting with a number, no other bracketed number after a blank. Function-call text glued to a word - `exit(1)`, `f(2)` - and a citation glued to a word stay quiet as today. A description with no marker word at all prints nothing.

MEASURE, AND REPORT IN THE OUTCOME. Walk every committed description in this repository (the previous clause task's walk script is where the orchestrator's brief says): how many hold a marker, how many print a line before and after, and each description that newly prints, by task id with its line. ITEMS CHANGED must be zero - the strict reading is not touched.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a), (b) and (c), red before the change. For the rule itself, a generated case: descriptions built from parts the case places - a marker in each spelling of a fixed table of strict and non-strict spellings, items in each numbering form, the forms mixed - where the case knows from its own construction how many items it wrote, and the assertion is the property: whenever the strict reading's count differs from the count written, a line is printed. The expectation comes from the construction, never from the reader. Allow twins, silent before and after: the plain list in each of the two styles; a list with wrapped item lines that do not start with a number; `exit(1)` and `f(2)` inside an item; a description with no marker word. The existing cases stay as they are unless one pins a detector this replaces; name each such case in the outcome with what it asserted and asserts now. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the wide reading made equal to the strict (each of (a) to (c) must go red); the comparison dropped; the normalisation dropped; the conservation check answering nothing; the cut of a quoted part removed (the timing case must go red or the child be killed).

NOT in this task: reading more spellings as the marker or more forms as openers in the STRICT reading - what a task is held to does not change; where the last item ends; the machine-readable form of the add verb.

Acceptance:
(1) Each of (a), (b) and (c) prints a line that gives the wide reading's count and the line where the readings part.
(2) The wide reading is the same reader called with the wide column of one table of choices.
(3) Over the generated descriptions, no description whose strict count differs from the count the case wrote is silent.
(4) The allow twins print nothing, and every description that printed a line before still prints one.
(5) The conservation check names a gap a case builds, and a reading whose check is silenced turns a case red.
(6) The reading's time grows about linearly at doubling lengths for many numbers, mentions and markers on one line, under the ceiling.
(7) The outcome carries the walk over the committed descriptions with ITEMS CHANGED zero and names each description that newly prints.
(8) The module, the conventions reference and the changelog state the rule and are true of the code.

tasks.title: The guard and the journal ask one function which file is the audit config, and each name is judged where it is looked up
tasks.description:
A fresh review of the config hold found no write let through on an ordinary checkout and no honest write held, and three things that are not as the documents say. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) THE JOURNAL ASKS A DIFFERENT QUESTION. The edit guard now answers which file a path names by identity and by the volume's rule on letter case; the write journal still decides that a write is a config edit by comparing the placed path with the config's spelling. For a write the guard asks the main session about - the project's config spelled in another case, a nested worktree's config, the same in another case - the journal records no config row at all, while the README says every config write leaves a hash-chained row. This predates the phase; the phase's own rule, one function for the question, is what it breaks.
(b) ONE DIRECTORY ANSWERS FOR ANOTHER. For a write that would create the file, the case rule is asked once, of an entry of the nearest existing directory on the path. Where the name that differs is looked up in a directory with another rule, the answer is wrong: with the config's folder present and telling case apart, inside a tree that does not, a write through the folder's name in another case is allowed and creates the real config. The reviewer built it with a mounted image; a folder with its own case setting inside a checkout is the same arrangement. The function's own docstring says a per-directory setting is answered by the directory the asked name sits in.
(c) THE CASE THAT HOLDS THE DISK-CALL CLAIM CANNOT FAIL FOR A LISTING. SECURITY.md says an ordinary write makes no more disk calls than before and names the case that measures it. That case counts three kinds of call and not a directory listing - the very call the new code makes. With the guard changed to list a directory on every ordinary write, the suite stays green.
(d) The README and the changelog say a hard link is the config with no exception; SECURITY.md and the code except a hard link to a NESTED tree's config under another name, and neither says that a hard link placed in the project to a config of a tree OUTSIDE it is not matched.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. ONE FUNCTION, TWO CALLERS. The question - does this path name the file a session in some tree of this repository would load as its audit config, and which way - is answered in one place both hooks can reach under the hook layer's import rule, and the journal classifies a write as a config edit by that answer and by nothing else. So the two cannot disagree: every write the guard holds as the config is, once made, a config row in the journal, and no other write is. The row keeps its existing shape; its path is the path as placed. The journal runs after the write and stays advisory: an error inside the question leaves the journal's fail mode as SECURITY.md's table states it, and the row for the project's own config spelled plainly is written exactly as today.
2. EACH NAME IS JUDGED WHERE IT IS LOOKED UP. For a creating write, the path is walked from the tree's root down, one component at a time. A component spelled as the config's is followed. A component that differs from the config's in letter case only is judged in the directory that holds it: where the config's own component exists there, the two are the same when both lookups reach one entry - identity, no rule needed; where it does not exist there, by that directory's own rule, asked of an entry of that directory as today; and where that directory holds no name that can answer, through the nearest directory above that can, as today, or held without regard to case with the stated words when none can. A directory the write would itself create has no rule yet and takes the answer of the directory it would be created in. A component that differs in more than case ends the walk: another file.
3. THE DISK-CALL CASE COUNTS EVERY CALL THAT ASKS THE DISK. The counter wraps, through one table in the case, every function of the os module the hook can reach that reads the filesystem - the three it counts today, a listing in each of its forms, and whatever else the hook file calls (derive the table's completeness in the case: every `os.` and `os.path.` call the hook's source makes is either in the table or in a short list of ones that touch no disk, and a call in neither turns the case red). The claim in SECURITY.md is then what the case measures, for an ordinary source write and for a file merely named like the config in a plain folder.
4. THE DOCUMENTS SAY WHAT IS AND IS NOT MATCHED, THE SAME IN EACH. README, changelog, SECURITY.md and the build guide agree on the hard-link exceptions of (d) and on the journal's row for a nested or case-variant config.

WHAT MUST STAY AS IT IS. Every answer the guard gives today on a volume with one case rule (the orchestrator's and the reviewers' probes, where the brief says) - same holds, same allows, same words. The disk calls of an ordinary write do not rise; the reviewer's independent count is in the brief. The hook import budget gate stays green. The fail-mode table's rows do not change.

HOW TO PROVE. For (a): through the journal hook run as a process over real linked worktrees, a row for each of the three writes it missed, red before; allow twins that write no config row - a file named like the config in a plain folder, in a worktree's docs, an ordinary source file. And one case that states the agreement itself: over a table of paths, the guard's answer is a hold exactly when the journal's classification is a config edit. For (b): a case that builds a directory telling case apart inside one that does not where the host can (a disk image on macOS, skipped by name with the reason elsewhere - and say in the outcome on which hosts it ran), plus a case through a stubbed per-directory answer that runs everywhere and shows each component is asked of its own directory. For (c): the mutation that lists a directory on every ordinary write turns the case red. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run, with those rows and: the journal put back to the spelling comparison; the walk collapsed to one question of the nearest existing directory; an allow row for each (the function widened until a plain folder's file is a config must turn a twin red).

NOT in this task: the shell route to the config, which stays journalled and not refused, as stated; Windows names with a trailing dot or blank; what the doctor says about the trail.

Acceptance:
(1) The journal writes a config row for the project's config spelled in another case, for a nested worktree's config, and for that in another case, and none for the allow twins.
(2) Over a table of paths, the guard holds a write exactly when the journal classifies it as a config edit, and both call one function.
(3) A creating write through a name differing in case is judged in the directory that holds that name, shown on a real pair of directories with different rules where the host can make one and through a stubbed per-directory answer everywhere.
(4) The disk-call case counts listings and every other call of the hook that asks the disk, goes red when an ordinary write lists a directory, and its table is held complete against the hook's source.
(5) Every answer the guard gave before on a volume with one case rule is unchanged, and an ordinary write makes no more disk calls than before.
(6) README, changelog, SECURITY.md and the build guide say the same about a hard link and about the journal's row, and are true of the code.
(7) The hook import budget gate is green and the fail-mode table is unchanged.

tasks.title: The floor guard calls a test moved only when no pairing of the code around it leaves it in place
tasks.description:
The last floor task made a test file compared only when the code outside its tests is identical and every existing test has a twin in the same position. Position was given to its executor as a count: the number of statements that are not tests standing before the test in its part. The executor built that, measured it, and reported what it does to honest edits; the orchestrator ran the same inputs.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) FALSE FINDINGS. One line of set-up added before an existing check makes every check after it a finding, moved, because each now has one more statement before it. The file is already listed as not compared, only added - that is the true answer and the whole of it. Over this repository's task commits the executor counted 274 commits that newly read as findings, 256 of them holding nothing but such moved findings (the count is in its measurement files, where the orchestrator's brief says). A finding is the guard's strongest word and here it is said of an edit that moved nothing.
(b) A MOVE THE COUNT CANNOT SEE. Each enclosing statement is named by its head, so a check moved from one block into a later block with an identical head - across a statement that clears the failures - reads clean. The executor found it and wrote it into the documents as a gap.
Both come from one cause: a count of statements is a position only when the statements counted are the same ones in both copies.

THE RULE TO BUILD. Position is defined by pairing, not by counting.
1. TOKENS. In each part of each copy (the module's body, a function's, a class's, each part of a compound statement) the statements that are not units form a sequence. A simple statement's token is its syntax; a compound statement's token is its head - its syntax with every nested statement list emptied.
2. A BEST PAIRING. For two sequences of tokens, a best pairing is a longest common subsequence. There can be more than one.
3. IN PLACE. A unit standing after i statements of the base part and after j of the tree part is in place when some best pairing of the two sequences pairs nothing across it: the longest common subsequence of the first i with the first j, plus that of the rest with the rest, equals that of the whole. A compound statement that encloses a unit is in place by the same test with itself as a paired member, and its parts are then compared part by part - body with body, else with else, each handler with the handler of the same place, finally with finally. A unit is IN THE SAME POSITION when every enclosing statement from the module down is in place and it is in place in the innermost part.
4. MOVED. A unit of the base copy whose twin by its own syntax stands in the tree copy and is not in the same position has moved: a finding, as today, saying from where to where. A unit whose twin is in the same position is compared. Two adjacent units swapped are both in place, since no statement that is not a unit stands between them.
5. THE REST. The rest is the same when at every level the two token sequences are equal; only added when at every level the base sequence is a subsequence of the tree's; changed or removed otherwise. These are the same pairings rule 3 uses - computed once, used for both answers - and the reason texts stay as they are.
So: a statement added before a unit leaves the unit in place (the file is not compared, only added, and nothing else is said); a unit moved across a statement, into another block, or into a later block with the same head is moved; and where the rest was changed or removed, a unit is still judged against the best pairing of what is there.

TIME. The pairing tables are computed once per pair of parts, forwards and backwards, so that each unit's test is a lookup. The guard reads this repository's largest test file, edited by one appended case, in time you measure and report; a case holds the reading of a generated file of several thousand statements and units under a ceiling, in a child killed at a deadline.

MEASURE, AND REPORT IN THE OUTCOME. The same walk over this repository's task commits, against the tree before this task and against the commit before the last floor task (b4492a27): the tally of verdicts; how many of the 256 moved-only commits still read findings and what each of those says (sample ten by hand and state for each whether the move is real); that no commit that read findings at b4492a27 lost one. Do not tune the rule to move the tally.

WHAT STAYS. Which statements are units; the cross-file rule; the reason texts; the filed block's shape; every answer on the third review's inputs and on the cases the last task added, unless a case pins the count this replaces - name each such case in the outcome with what it asserted and asserts now.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for (a): a set-up line before an existing check, in a row suite and in a unittest method's class - not compared, only added, no finding. tasks.title: The floor guard sets aside only a label's literal text and a bare new test's body, and says so in one table
tasks.description:
A fourth review of the floor guard, over the two tasks that rebuilt it around structural identity, found no regression, no finding on an honest edit of this repository's suites, and every move across statements and blocks it tried. It also found four places where the comparison still sets something aside by its KIND, and for each an edit confined to that kind after which a failing test passes while the reading is clean. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator; each reads clean on the tree before those tasks too, so none is a regression.

MEASURED (answer clean, nothing listed as not compared).
(a) WHAT A LABEL INTERPOLATES. Only a label's constant text is kept and nothing compares the expressions it formats in: a format value that rebinds the variable the condition reads, one that clears the recorded failures, one that ends the run, and a constant label turned into a formatted one carrying a call (read as a rename). A case in the suite pins this as intended.
(b) A NEW TEST'S DEFINITION. A new test definition is taken out whole, so what runs when it is DEFINED is read by nobody: a decorator that rebinds an existing test's name in the class body, a decorator or a default that replaces the check function or an assertion method, a new definition under the name of a table an existing test loops over. The documents say only that a new test can do anything when it RUNS.
(c) DOCSTRINGS. They are dropped from the rest and from each test, so a doctest whose expected output is edited to pass, or whose failing example is deleted, reads clean.
(d) A DECORATOR'S FIRST ARGUMENT. The expected-failure marker's first positional argument is blanked as if it were a reason; for that marker it is the condition, and a string condition made always true reads clean with no skip finding.

THE RULE TO BUILD. What the comparison does not compare is stated once, as a table in the module, and has exactly these rows; everything else of both copies is compared, by S for the rest and by U for a unit.
1. THE LITERAL TEXT OF A LABEL. A unit's own syntax is all of it but the constant text of its label. Every expression a label formats, interpolates or joins is compared like the condition. A label whose literal text alone changed stays a rename; a label whose values changed is a change of the unit, and the finding says WHICH part of the unit differs - what it is called through, its condition and arguments, or the values its label carries - so that a reviewer can tell an edited condition from an edited message.
2. THE BODY OF A BARE NEW TEST. A new unit is a test definition under a name the base copy mentions nowhere, with nothing evaluated when it is defined - no decorator, no default, no annotation that is evaluated - or a new labelled check statement, as today. Only such a definition's BODY is set aside. A new test definition that is not bare, or whose name the base copy mentions, is not a new unit: its head stays in the rest, so the file is listed as not compared, only added, naming it. A definition nested in a helper is named for what it is and not as a test of the class.
3. A DOCSTRING HOLDING NO EXAMPLE. A docstring is set aside only when neither copy's text of it holds a doctest prompt. One that does is syntax of the statement holding it: of a unit (a changed example is a change of the unit) or of the rest.
4. A REASON, WHERE THE DECORATOR'S OWN SIGNATURE CALLS IT ONE. For each skip or expected-failure decorator the guard knows, the argument set aside is the one that decorator documents as its reason, by position or by keyword; any other argument is compared. The expected-failure marker's first positional argument is a condition.
Nothing else is set aside. If the module sets aside anything this table does not name, it is either added to the table with the reason it cannot change what runs, or it is compared - say which in the outcome.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS SAY. The module, the build guide, the README row and the changelog carry the table's four rows in words, and one sentence on what the reading is: a comparison of structure that never evaluates code, so a new test or a new check can do anything when it runs, and an author set on defeating it can; clean means every existing test stands where it stood, unchanged, and nothing but tests was touched.

WHAT THIS COSTS, AND YOU MEASURE IT. A new decorated or parametrised test now makes its file not compared; an existing check whose message gained a value is now a finding that says so. Run the measurement over this repository's task commits before and after and report the tally, how many commits changed verdict and in which direction, and ten of them judged by hand. Do not tune the rule to move the tally.

CASES THAT PIN WHAT THIS REPLACES are changed on purpose - the one that pins a label's values as unread among them; name each in the outcome with what it asserted and asserts now.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each measured input of (a) to (d), red before the change. The invariant case gains operators - a value inside a label edited, a decorator added to a new test, a default added to a new test, a new test under a name the base copy mentions, a doctest example edited in a unit's docstring and in the module's - and its own route sets aside exactly the table's rows by its own means, so that it would disagree with the guard if the guard set aside more. Allow twins, clean before and after: a label's literal text reworded; a bare new test method; a bare new test function; a docstring with no example reworded, in a unit and in the module; a skip reason reworded by keyword and by position. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: one row per table row removed from the comparison (each of (a) to (d) goes red) and one per table row widened (its allow twin goes red).

NOT in this task: other languages; evaluating what code does; which reading a file gets; the wording of a moved finding for a renamed enclosing function.

Acceptance:
(1) Each measured input of (a) to (d) is a finding or a file listed as not compared with the statement named, and none reads clean.
(2) A finding for a changed unit says whether its callee, its condition and arguments, or its label's values differ.
(3) A new test definition with a decorator, a default or an evaluated annotation, or under a name the base copy mentions, leaves its head in the rest; a bare one under a fresh name is a new unit.
(4) A docstring holding a doctest prompt in either copy is compared; one holding none is not.
(5) The module states what is set aside in one table with these four rows and sets aside nothing else.
(6) The allow twins read clean.
(7) The invariant case sets aside the table's rows by its own means, agrees with the guard on every generated edit, and goes red when the guard sets aside more.
(8) The outcome carries the measurement, the verdict changes with ten judged by hand, and each existing case changed on purpose.
(9) The module, the build guide, the README row and the changelog state the four rows and what a clean reading means, and are true of the code.

tasks.title: Green-first proves by the same difference for a test file HEAD already holds
tasks.description:
The last green-first task made proved a difference between two runs of the same new test file, with the task's own test definitions and without them. For a declared test file that HEAD already holds it was told to keep HEAD's copy as the baseline, on the argument that what the task added is then already the difference. That argument is false, the task's executor said so in its hand-back, and the orchestrator ran it through the real green verb on git fixtures.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands, each a task that edits a test file HEAD holds and adds no new one; each answers proved with no case of the task's own having run and passed:
(a) the file gains a subclass of a HEAD test class and a test method in a plain class the runner never collects;
(b) it gains two subclasses of a HEAD class and a class of own cases skipped as a class on the base;
(c) it gains a subclass with an own case the command deselects by name;
(d) it gains a subclass with an own case under a skip decorator bound to another name.
In each the rise between HEAD's copy and the task's copy is the HEAD class's inherited cases collected again - the same hole the last task closed for a new file. The same file gaining only an empty subclass is refused today, and a passing own case added to a HEAD class, to a new class or to a subclass is proved today; both stay.

THE RULE TO BUILD. One baseline for every declared Python test file, new at HEAD or not: the task's copy of the file with the task's own test definitions taken out - by the function the last task built, with the same reading of which definitions are the task's own (not identical to a definition of the same name and class chain in HEAD's tree). The task's run is as today. Proved is the passed count rising between those two runs, because nothing but the task's own definitions differs between them. The count argument - definitions against skips - is no longer used for any file whose definitions can be taken out; it stays only for the runners the module already names as ones whose definitions it cannot take out, labelled the weaker proof as today.
What follows, and is stated in the module and the document: the baseline is no longer HEAD's own copy of an edited test file, so a task that changes a helper in that file in a way that breaks HEAD's cases on HEAD's code gets a baseline that is not green and the answer could-not-prove with the runner's line - where the task's own run of the same file is not also failing, which is not-green first. And the two limits of the last task hold for an existing file as for a new one.

WHAT STAYS. The red verb and its baseline. Every answer for a NEW file (the previous probes, where the orchestrator's brief says). The payload's shape and keys. The house and sweep routes.

HOW TO PROVE. A case for each of (a) to (d) through the real green verb on a git fixture, red before the change. Allow twins through the real verb, proved before and after: a passing case added to a HEAD class; a new class with one passing case added to the file; a subclass of a HEAD class with one passing own case; two own cases, one skipped and one passing. Still not-green: a case added to the file that fails on the base. Still could-not-prove: the file gaining only an empty subclass. One case for what follows from the rule: a helper changed so that HEAD's cases fail on HEAD's code, with the answer and its basis. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the existing-file baseline put back to HEAD's copy (a case of (a) to (d) goes red); the count argument put back for an existing file; an allow row (the difference refused for an existing file turns a twin red).

NOT in this task: jest, vitest and playwright; whether could-not-prove stops a sign-off; the schema's wording of the field.

Acceptance:
(1) Each of (a) to (d) is could-not-prove through the real verb, its basis naming the definitions taken out and the two counts.
(2) Every declared Python test file, new or held by HEAD, gets the same baseline: the task's copy with the task's own definitions taken out.
(3) The allow twins are proved, the failing case is not-green and the empty subclass is could-not-prove, as before.
(4) The answers for a new file and the red verb's answers are unchanged.
(5) A helper change that breaks HEAD's cases on HEAD's code is answered as the rule says, shown by a case.
(6) The module, the build guide, the changelog and the reference document state one baseline and are true of the code.

tasks.title: Green-first's two runs hold the same files, and its basis says only what the runs measured
tasks.description:
A fresh review of the two tasks that made green-first a difference between two runs found the removal of a task's own definitions right on every file shape it tried, the red verb unchanged and every honest new file proved. It found three regressions, none in the unsafe direction; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator through the real green verb on a git fixture.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) THE TWO RUNS DO NOT HOLD THE SAME FILES. A task renames a test file and adds one case; it declares both paths, the old one deleted and the new one holding HEAD's cases and the added one. The answer is could-not-prove, with a passed count that FELL between the runs; before the two tasks it was proved. The task's run lays over every declared path and deletes the one the task deleted; the baseline run is built only from the declared test files still present in the working tree, so HEAD's copy of the deleted file stays in it and its cases are counted twice.
(b) THE BASIS NAMES CASES AS SEEN THAT NEVER RAN. A proved basis lists every definition taken out for the baseline as the task's own cases seen: a case the command deselected, and one skipped on the base, are named beside the one that ran. The count is right; the names are not what the sentence says they are.
(c) THE BASIS BLAMES HEAD FOR THE TASK'S OWN FILE. A new test file that imports the task's new code at module level cannot load on the base, trimmed or not. The answer could-not-prove is right and the runner's line is there, but the basis opens by saying HEAD's own tests are not green, that the command is already red at HEAD, and to narrow it to the task's cases - none of which is true, and narrowing changes nothing. The sentence is reworded today only for a file HEAD holds.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. ONE SET OF PATHS, LAID THE SAME WAY IN BOTH RUNS. The two runs are built from one list: every path the task declares, test file or not, as the task's run lays it today - present ones laid over, deleted ones deleted. The baseline differs from the task's run in exactly one thing: each declared Python test file that is present is laid with the task's own definitions taken out. The verb checks it rather than assuming it: after both trees are laid, the set of paths that differ between them is exactly the set of files something was taken out of, and a difference outside that set is a could-not-prove that names the path.
2. THE BASIS SAYS WHAT WAS TAKEN OUT AND WHAT ROSE, AND CLAIMS NOTHING ABOUT WHICH DEFINITION RAN. The names are the definitions taken out for the baseline, called that; the proof is that the passed count rose by a stated number between two runs that differ in nothing else, so at least that many of them ran and passed. No sentence says a named definition was seen, ran or passed unless the run's own output names it.
3. A BASELINE THAT FAILS BECAUSE OF A FILE THE TASK LAID IS SAID TO BE THAT. Where the baseline's failure is in a declared file - it did not load, or a case in it failed - the basis says the task's own file, with its own definitions taken out, did not load or fails on HEAD's code, gives the runner's line, and says what that means: its cases cannot pass before the change. The sentence about HEAD's own tests being red and the advice to narrow the command are printed only when the failure is in a file the task did not lay.

WHAT STAYS. Every status the previous probes got (where the orchestrator's brief says), except (a), which becomes proved. The red verb. The payload's shape and keys. The two stated limits.

HOW TO PROVE. Through the real green verb on git fixtures, red before: a renamed test file with one added case is proved by a rise of one; a test file split in two with one added case likewise; a declared test file only deleted is could-not-prove with nothing of its own to take out and a count that did not fall; a proved basis for a run that deselected one own case and skipped another names the definitions as taken out and does not call any of them seen; a new file importing new code at module level says its own file did not load on HEAD's code and carries neither the sentence about HEAD's tests nor the advice to narrow. One case for the check of rule 1: a baseline made to keep a path the task's run deletes is refused naming the path. Allow twin: a command that really is red at HEAD in a file the task did not touch still gets the sentence about HEAD and the advice. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the baseline built from the present files only (the rename case goes red); the check of rule 1 dropped; the names called seen again; the HEAD sentence printed for a laid file; and the allow row (the HEAD sentence dropped for an untouched file turns the twin red).

NOT in this task: the lows of the same review; other runners; whether could-not-prove stops a sign-off.

Acceptance:
(1) A renamed test file with one added case, and a split one, are proved by the difference.
(2) Both runs are built from one list of declared paths and the verb refuses, naming the path, when the two trees differ outside the files something was taken out of.
(3) No basis says a named definition ran, passed or was seen unless the run's own output names it; a proved basis names what was taken out and the rise.
(4) A baseline failing in a file the task laid says so with the runner's line; the sentence about HEAD's own tests and the advice to narrow are printed only for a failure in a file the task did not lay.
(5) Every other status of the previous probes and of the red verb is unchanged.
(6) The module, the build guide, the changelog and the reference document say what the basis now says and are true of the code.

tasks.title: The wider Acceptance reading takes a bare word as a marker only where a list opens under it, and its line quotes text
tasks.description:
A fresh review of the task that made the Acceptance reading silent only when a wider reading agrees found the strict reading untouched - no item differs over every committed description and a large generated set - time linear, and the measured departures now said. It found three defects in the wider reading itself; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A PLAIN DESCRIPTION NOW PRINTS A LINE. In the wider reading the marker word at a line start counts as a marker with or without its colon. So an item that wraps onto a line beginning with the word, or a closing paragraph beginning with it, opens a second marker, cuts the list short, and the write says a wider reading finds FEWER items; a description with no marker at all and one prose line beginning with the word is told a wider reading finds an item. None of these printed before that task. Over generated plain parenthesised lists hard-wrapped at a fixed width, about a quarter print once the word is in the vocabulary; none did before.
(b) THE LINE POINTS AT A BLANK LINE AND QUOTES NOTHING. Where a blank line, or a line of blanks, sits between the list and the place the readings part, the line names the blank line and quotes an empty string - for the measured shape itself, a parenthesised list continued by another numbering after a blank line.
(c) NOTHING PINS THE SECOND HALF OF THE COMPARISON. The write is silent only when the wider reading finds the same count AND the same text. With the text half removed - silent whenever the counts are equal - every case of the suite passes, and the one committed description that the task made print, whose two readings both count six, goes quiet.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. A BARE WORD IS A MARKER ONLY WHERE A LIST OPENS UNDER IT. In the wider reading the marker word with its colon counts as today. Without a colon it counts only when a list opens directly under it: the first text after the word - on the rest of its line or on the next line holding text - is an item opener numbered one, in any form the wider reading knows. A line that merely begins with the word is prose. This is one row of the table of choices, not a second scanner.
2. THE PARTING LINE HOLDS TEXT. The line named is the first line HOLDING TEXT that the two readings place differently, numbered in the description as written, and its quote is never empty.
3. EQUAL COUNTS ARE SAID AS THAT. When the two readings find the same number of items with different text, the line says so in those words - the same number, placed differently - and does not report the count as if it were a difference.

WHAT STAYS. The strict reading, to the character. Every line that printed before the previous task. Every measured departure that task made print still prints. The two older detectors. Time linear in the text.

HOW TO PROVE. Cases, red before: a list item wrapping onto a line that begins with the word, in both cases of its first letter and with emphasis around it, is silent; a closing paragraph beginning with the word, after a blank line and after none, is silent; a description with no marker and a prose line beginning with the word is silent; a heading or a label holding the word with no colon and a list numbered from one under it still prints; a parenthesised list continued by each other numbering after one blank line, after two, after a line of blanks, and with carriage-return line ends, names the continuing line and quotes its text; a description whose two readings count the same and differ in text prints, in the words of rule 3. The generated case gains a plain half: plain lists built from parts, their prose drawn from a vocabulary that holds the word in both cases and wrapped at several widths, with the expectation computed from the construction - silent unless a wrapped line begins with a number and its opener, which the construction knows. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the bare word counted at any line start (the plain half and the wrap cases go red); the parting line taken from blank lines too; the text half of the comparison removed; and an allow row (the bare word never counted turns the heading and label cases red).

NOT in this task: openers and markers the wider reading does not hold; the reading's JSON form; the lows of the same review.

Acceptance:
(1) A line that only begins with the marker word - in an item, after the list, or in a description with no marker - prints nothing, and generated plain lists holding the word print nothing.
(2) A bare word with a list numbered from one opening under it is still read as a marker by the wider reading.
(3) The parting line named holds text and the quote is that text, with blank lines and carriage returns between.
(4) Readings that count the same and differ in text print a line that says so, and a case fails when the text half of the comparison is removed.
(5) The strict reading and every line printed before the previous task are unchanged over the committed descriptions.
(6) The module, the conventions document, the build guide and the changelog say when a bare word is a marker and are true of the code.

tasks.title: Green-first says why its baseline is not green from a run of HEAD's own tree, not from where the failure lies
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made green-first's two runs hold the same files found no honest task refused, every status right, the check refusing what it says it refuses, and the red verb unchanged. It found the sentence about a baseline that is not green wrong in two ways; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator through the real green verb on git fixtures. The statuses are right in every one; only the words are wrong.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands. The verb decides what to say about a baseline that is not green from the FILE the failure lies in: in a file the task laid, it says the task's own file fails or did not load on HEAD's code, so the cases in it cannot pass before the change; elsewhere, that the command is red at HEAD and to narrow it.
(a) A case of HEAD's own, red at HEAD, in a test file the task adds a passing case to: the basis says the task's own file fails on HEAD's code and that its cases cannot pass before the change, and the advice to narrow is gone. Both halves are false - the failing case is HEAD's and unchanged, and the same task with the command narrowed to its case is proved. Before the previous task the basis said the command was red at HEAD and to narrow it. The same for a file of HEAD's that already fails to load at HEAD.
(b) A new test file that imports, at module level, a helper the task also adds under a test-like name: taking the task's definitions out removes the helper, the file does not load, and the basis says its cases cannot pass before the change - with the import moved into the case, the same case is proved. The sentence no longer names the helper's file as one something was taken out of.
(c) A new test file importing an untouched module that raises: the basis says its cases cannot pass before the change; they cannot pass after it either.
(d) A declared path that is in neither tree is said to be deleted by the task.
By construction a case that fails in the baseline is never one of the task's own - those were taken out - so where a failure lies cannot tell whose it is.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE CAUSE IS MEASURED. When the baseline is not green - a case failed or a module did not load - the verb runs the same command once more on HEAD's own tree with nothing of the task's laid, and words the cause by that run's answer:
- red there too: the command is red at HEAD without anything of the task's, with that run's line, and the advice to narrow the command to the task's cases;
- green there: the command is green at HEAD and stops being green once the declared files are laid with the task's own definitions taken out, with the baseline's line and the files something was taken out of - what is left of them fails or does not load on HEAD's code. No sentence says what the task's cases can or cannot do before the change, and there is no advice to narrow;
- not readable, or past its deadline: the basis says the cause was not measured and why.
The extra run happens only on this path, under the same isolation and deadline as the other two, and the basis names it as a run. The status does not depend on it.
2. A PATH IS CALLED DELETED ONLY WHEN HEAD HOLDS IT. A declared path in neither tree is said to be absent from both.
3. THE CHECK OF THE TWO LAID TREES SAYS WHAT IT READS. The documents say the check compares the declared paths of the two trees - which is what it does - and not a difference anywhere. The half of the check that refuses a file something was taken out of yet does not differ either gets a case that fails without it, through the seam the other half is tested by, or is removed with the reason stated.

WHAT STAYS. Every status of every earlier probe (the orchestrator's brief says where). The red verb, to the character. The payload's shape and keys. The two runs of a green baseline, and the number of runs when the baseline is green.

HOW TO PROVE. Through the real green verb on git fixtures, red before: for each of (a), both shapes - the basis says the command is red at HEAD and advises narrowing, and does not call the file the task's own failure; for (b) and (c) and for a new file importing the change's new code at module level - the basis says green at HEAD, not green with the declared files laid, names the files something was taken out of, and carries neither the advice nor a sentence on what the cases can do; for (d) - absent from both. One case for the third answer of rule 1, with the extra run made unreadable through the seam. One case that a green baseline makes exactly two runs. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the cause decided by where the failure lies again; the extra run skipped and its answer assumed green; assumed red; a path in neither tree called deleted; and an allow row - the extra run made on every baseline turns the two-runs case red.

NOT in this task: the other lows of the same review; other runners; whether could-not-prove stops a sign-off.

Acceptance:
(1) A baseline that is not green is explained by a run of HEAD's own tree: red there says the command is red at HEAD and advises narrowing; green there says the declared files as laid fail or do not load on HEAD's code and names the files something was taken out of.
(2) No basis says what the task's cases can or cannot do before the change.
(3) When the extra run cannot be read the basis says the cause was not measured.
(4) A green baseline makes two runs and no third.
(5) A declared path in neither tree is called absent from both.
(6) The documents say the check of the two laid trees reads the declared paths, and each half of that check either has a case that fails without it or is gone.
(7) Every status of the earlier probes and the red verb's output are unchanged.
(8) The module, the build guide, the changelog and the reference document say how the cause is found and are true of the code.

tasks.title: A colon-less Acceptance label is read the same way whether its list opens on its own line or the next
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the wider Acceptance reading take a bare marker word only where a list opens under it found the strict reading untouched, every line printed before the wider reading existed still printed, plain prose quiet, the parting line always holding text, and time linear. It found one asymmetry, run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands. Under a colon-less label of more than one word, a list on the NEXT line is read by the wider reading and the write says so; the same list on the label's OWN line is read by neither reading and nothing is printed - the task is held to no clause in silence. `Acceptance criteria` followed by a line-break and a two-item list prints; the same label followed by a blank and the same list does not, in every numbering form. The function that decides whether a list opens under the bare word accepts, on the word's own line, an opener only as the first thing after the word, and across a line break allows label words before it. The commit before that task said the same-line shape.

THE RULE TO BUILD. One rule for both places. After the bare word, words of a label may stand before the opener numbered one, on the word's own line as across the line break. On the word's own line, where a reference in prose and a list look alike, label words are allowed only when the list goes on: an opener numbered two, in the same form, follows the opener numbered one. An opener numbered one directly after the word stays a list as today.
Stated in the module and the conventions document as limits, not built: a bare label is read only over a list numbered from one - a colon-less heading over a list that starts at another number or is quoted or emphasised is not read and nothing is said; and a reference numbered one directly after the word in prose is read as a list.

WHAT STAYS. The strict reading, to the character. Every line that printed before the wider reading existed. Prose stays quiet: the share of generated plain lists that print does not rise for the vocabularies that hold the word. Time linear.

HOW TO PROVE. Cases, red before: each multi-word colon-less label the review used, with a two-item list on its own line in each numbering form, prints; the allow side, silent before and after - a prose line that begins with the word and holds one bracketed reference numbered one later in the line; a prose line beginning with the word and holding a version number; the word followed by an opener numbered one inside a code fence on the next line (no case pins that fence check today: removing it leaves the suite green). NOT in this task: lists under a bare label that do not start at one; other openers and markers the wider reading does not hold.

Acceptance:
(1) A colon-less label of several words with a list of two or more items on its own line is read by the wider reading and the write says so, in every numbering form the wider reading knows.
(2) A prose line beginning with the marker word and holding a single reference numbered one later in the line prints nothing.
(3) The fence check on the next-line path has a case that fails without it.
(4) The strict reading and every line printed before the wider reading existed are unchanged over the committed descriptions, and the share of generated plain lists that print has not risen.
(5) The module and the conventions document state the rule and its two limits and are true of the code.

tasks.title: Green-first states what its two baseline runs showed and names the cause as one of two readings
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made green-first explain a baseline that is not green by one more run of HEAD's own tree found the status independent of that run under every forced answer, the three answers true on every deterministic input, the run count and the deadline right, and the red verb unchanged. It found one sentence that states more than one extra run can establish; it was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator through the real green verb on a git fixture.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands. HEAD holds a test that fails on its first invocation only; the task adds a new passing test file. The baseline run is red in HEAD's flaky test, the extra run is green, and the basis says the command is green at HEAD and stops being green once the declared files are laid - that what is left of the task's new file fails or does not load on HEAD's code. The new file loaded and holds no case after the take-out; the only failure is in a file nothing was laid into, and the basis's own first clause names it. One green run after one red run cannot tell a failure the laid files cause from a command that does not give the same answer twice. The status, could-not-prove, is right. Placement cannot settle it either - a laid file that changes shared state turns an untouched file red every time - so the answer is in the words.
Two smaller things in the same sentence: the extra run is described as HEAD's own tree with nothing of the task's laid, while it lays each new declared test file as an empty stub, which matters when the command names such a file by path; and an exception raised inside the extra run aborts the verb instead of leaving the cause unmeasured.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. TWO OBSERVATIONS, THEN TWO READINGS. When the extra run is green, the basis says what the two runs showed - not green with the declared files laid, with the baseline's own line; green on one run of HEAD's own tree - and then that this has two readings and the runs do not choose between them: what was laid causes the failure, or the command does not give the same answer twice. It names the files something was taken out of as what was laid, and says nothing as fact about which of them fails or does not load beyond what the baseline's own line names.
2. When the extra run is red, the basis says the command was red on a run of HEAD's own tree as well, with that run's line, and gives the advice to narrow, as today.
3. THE EXTRA RUN IS DESCRIBED AS IT IS LAID: HEAD's own tree with each new declared test file as an empty stub and nothing else of the task's.
4. AN EXTRA RUN THAT RAISES leaves the cause unmeasured, with the exception's name, like one that cannot be read or runs past its deadline. The status does not change.

WHAT STAYS. Every status of every earlier probe. The red verb, to the character. The payload's shape and keys. The run count: two for a green baseline, a third only when it is not green.

HOW TO PROVE. Through the real green verb on git fixtures, red before: a test of HEAD's that fails on its first invocation only, with a new passing test file - the basis gives both readings and does not say the new file fails or does not load; the same with the test failing in the extra run too - red on HEAD's own tree, the advice. Through the seam the suite stubs: an extra run that raises gives the not-measured answer with the exception's name, and the status is what it is without it. One case that the description of the extra run names the stubs when a new declared test file exists and does not when none does. The earlier cases for a file that does not load on HEAD's code keep their statuses and now assert the two readings. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the cause stated as fact again; the exception left to abort; the stubs left unsaid; and an allow row - the two readings printed for a red extra run turns the red case red.

NOT in this task: running the command more than once to tell the two readings apart; other runners; whether could-not-prove stops a sign-off.

Acceptance:
(1) A baseline that is not green with a green extra run is said as two observations and two readings, and no sentence states as fact that a laid file fails or does not load beyond what the baseline's own line names.
(2) A red extra run says the command was red on a run of HEAD's own tree and advises narrowing.
(3) The extra run is described with the empty stubs it lays.
(4) An extra run that raises leaves the cause unmeasured and the status unchanged.
(5) Every status of the earlier probes, the run count and the red verb's output are unchanged.
(6) The module, the build guide, the changelog and the reference document say what the basis now says and are true of the code.
