tasks.title: The config hold names the file a session would load, also when the config's folder is a symlink
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that gave the edit guard and the journal one question found every verdict and every word unchanged over a large table of writes, the per-directory case rule right on real volumes, and no crash. It also found a hole that is older than that task and lives in the function it moved; the reviewer ran it and the orchestrator ran it again, the hook as a process over a real repository.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) The project's config folder is a symlink to a directory OUTSIDE the repository and no config exists yet. A subagent writes the config, plainly spelled, with the plan gate switched off. The guard allows it, the journal writes no row, and the loader then reads the switch as off. The same write again, the file now existing, is allowed too. The question which tree a path belongs to places the resolved path outside the project before the config question is asked at all.
(b) The same with the folder a symlink to a directory INSIDE the project: allowed, where the commit before the task that made the question one of identity held it. The branch for a write that would create the file compares the resolved path of the write with a config path that was never resolved.
The documents say the config is matched through a symlink.

THE RULE TO BUILD. The property, stated as what can be tested by doing: the guard holds a write exactly when, once the write is made, the loader - asked for the project, for the tree the session stands in, or for the tree the path as written lies in - would read the written file as that tree's audit config. Built so:
1. THE CANDIDATE TREES do not depend on where the path resolves to: the project, the session's tree, the tree the path lies in as written, and the tree it lies in once resolved.
2. FOR EACH CANDIDATE the write's file and the tree's config are compared resolved against resolved. Where the tree's config exists, by identity, as today. Where it does not, the directory the write would create the file in and the tree's config folder are the same directory by identity once both are resolved, and the name is the config's by that directory's own rule on letter case, as the per-directory rule already says; where the folder itself does not exist, the walk of the previous task applies to the resolved path.
3. The journal asks the same function, so the row follows.

WHAT STAYS. Every verdict and every word on every write the review's table and the orchestrator's inputs hold today (the brief says where), except the measured inputs, which become holds. A file merely named like the config in a plain folder, an ordinary source file, and a write outside every tree to a file no tree loads are allowed as today. No directory listing on an ordinary write. The fail-mode table. The hook import budget.
The disk calls of an ordinary write may rise by what resolving each candidate tree's config path costs and by nothing else; the case that counts them is re-pinned to the new sequence and the outcome carries the count before and after.

HOW TO PROVE. One case that states the property by doing: over a table of arrangements - the config folder a real directory, a symlink inside the project, a symlink outside the repository, a symlink to another tree's config folder, a dangling symlink; the config present and absent; the write spelled through the link and spelled at the link's destination; main session and subagent - the hook's verdict is a hold exactly when, with the write made in the fixture, the loader reads the written content for one of the candidate trees. Red before for (a) and (b), each as the hook run as a process. Allow twins: a write into a symlinked folder that is NOT any tree's config folder; a file beside the config in the symlinked folder under another name. The journal's agreement case gains the symlinked arrangements. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the candidates narrowed to the tree the resolved path lies in; the creating comparison put back to an unresolved config path; and an allow row - any write into a symlinked folder held - turns the twins red.

NOT in this task: a symlink FILE in the project that points at the config of a worktree outside it; a hard link to the project's config placed in an outside worktree; the shell route. Each is stated in the documents as not matched.

Acceptance:
(1) With the config folder a symlink, inside the project or outside the repository, a subagent's write of the config is refused and the main session's is asked, whether or not the config exists yet and whether the write is spelled through the link or at its destination.

tasks.title: A config row names the file it recorded, so the trail check does not warn about an edit the journal saw
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the journal write a config row for every write the edit guard holds found the guard and the journal in agreement over every write it made, and two false warnings that task introduced in the trail check. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator: the hooks as processes, then the trail check.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands. The journal records a config row with its target spelled as the write placed it; the trail check anchors its drift warning on the target's spelling.
(a) The project's config is written plainly, then through its folder's name in another letter case on a volume that folds case, then plainly again. After the last write the trail check warns that the other-case spelling has changed since the last row that recorded it - an edit the journal never saw - though every one of the three writes has its row. The warning clears only when someone writes through the other spelling again. The doctor prints it as drift from outside: a checkout, a script, a shell write.
(b) The main session writes the config of a worktree nested under the project; the row goes into the project's trail. A session inside that worktree then edits its own config, recorded in that worktree's own trail - and the project's trail check warns of an edit the journal never saw. After the worktree is removed, the project warns that the file no longer exists and nothing clears it. Before that task there was no warning at any of these steps. Nested worktrees are where agent worktrees live, and removing them is routine.
The documents say nothing of either.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE TARGET IS THE FILE, NOT THE SPELLING. When the written file is the audit config of the tree whose trail the row goes into, the row's target is that config's own path as the journal has always written it, whatever spelling, letter case or symlink the write went through. The slot the journal keeps per target follows the same name, so a write through one spelling and the next through another are one file to it.
2. ANOTHER TREE'S CONFIG IS RECORDED AND IS NOT AN ANCHOR. A write to the config of a tree other than the one whose trail the row goes into is still a config row - the record that this session wrote there - with its target as placed. The trail check does not anchor drift on it: that file's own trail is its own tree's, so its later changes and its removal are not this trail's to warn about. The check decides this from the row and the tree, by the function that answers which file a path names - not from the spelling.
3. The warning for the tree's own config changed with no row is unchanged, and still fires when the config really is edited behind the journal.

WHAT STAYS. The row's shape and keys; a key may be added, none renamed or removed. The row for the project's own config written plainly, byte for byte apart from time and chain fields. Every other finding and warning of the trail check. The guard.

HOW TO PROVE. The hooks run as processes over a real repository with a nested worktree, then the trail check, red before: the three writes of (a) end with no warning; the three steps of (b) end with no warning at each step. Deny twins that must still warn: the project's own config edited with no hook run (a shell write) after a row; the same after a row recorded through the other-case spelling; the project's own config deleted after a row. One case that the slot follows the file: a write through the other spelling and then a plain one each record the state before as the other left it. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run: the target as placed again for the tree's own config; another tree's row anchored again; and an allow row - no config row anchored at all - turns the deny twins red.

NOT in this task: a write of a nested tree's config through an MCP tool, which leaves no row, as the documents state; the long relative target recorded for a write through an alias of the temp directory.

Acceptance:
(1) A config row for the trail's own tree names the config's own path whatever spelling or link the write went through, and the per-target slot follows it.
(2) After writes of the project's config through two spellings the trail check prints no warning.
(3) A row for another tree's config is recorded and is not a drift anchor: no warning when that tree's own session edits it or when the tree is removed.
(4) The project's own config edited or deleted behind the journal still warns, also after a row recorded through another spelling.
(5) The plain row is unchanged apart from time and chain fields, and no key is renamed or removed.
(6) SECURITY.md, the README, the changelog and the build guide say what a config row's target is and which rows the trail check anchors on, and are true of the code.

tasks.title: A new test is set aside only where the base copy cannot have bound its name, and the guard's own case fails when it sets aside more than its table
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that put what the floor guard sets aside into one table found every earlier measured input caught, the quiet direction quiet, and every mutation that stops a row being set aside or widens the bare-new-test row caught. It found two things; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) THE NAME BOUND WITHOUT BEING SPELLED. The base copy creates tests by computed name - a loop assigning into the module's globals, or a class body assigning into its locals under a string - and one of them fails. The tree adds a bare new test under that name. The guard reads the diff clean, and run side by side the base copy has a failing test and the tree copy has none. The row for a bare new test says it binds a name the base copy spells nowhere and so cannot change what runs; the module reads identifiers only, and the name here is a string or is computed.
(b) THE CASE THAT HOLDS THE TABLE DOES NOT SEE A WIDENING. With the module made to set aside more than the table says - an assertion's expected value treated as a reason; a reason's whole argument blanked, values included; a skip matched by its last dotted part under any receiver - the suite stays green, every case. Two of those are not equivalent: with them an existing test's expected value changed, or a call inside a skip reason's value, reads clean. The case's own route sets aside more than the table does, and it has no operator that touches a call argument that is not a reason. The comment beside the audited-exemption row says this case is what holds the module to its rows.
(c) A document sentence: a check whose message gained a value is said to be a finding naming its label's values; it is reported as the check gone, because the literal text is what names a check and gaining a value changes it.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. A NEW DEFINITION IS SET ASIDE ONLY WHERE THE BASE COPY CANNOT HAVE BOUND ITS NAME. Two readings of the base copy decide it. The name appears in the base copy as an identifier OR inside any string constant: the new definition is no unit. The base copy binds names by computation in the scope the new definition lands in - a subscript store into the result of a call to globals, locals or vars, a setattr call, a class made by a call to type, an exec or eval call: no new definition in that scope is a unit, whatever its name. In both the file is not compared, named with the reason, as for a new test that is not bare today. The row's reason in the table says this and no more.
2. THE CASE THAT HOLDS THE TABLE FAILS WHEN THE MODULE SETS ASIDE MORE THAN THE ROWS SAY. Its own comparison sets aside exactly what each row says - a reason's literal text and not its values, the listed skip forms under the receivers the module names and no other - and its generated edits include, for each row, an edit just OUTSIDE the row: a non-reason argument of a call changed, a value inside a reason changed, a skip-named call under another receiver changed, a number inside a label changed. Each such edit must be a finding or not compared.
3. THE DOCUMENTS SAY WHAT IS REPORTED when a label gains a value: the check is reported gone and the new label is listed as new.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer on every input of the earlier probes and of the orchestrator's inputs (the brief says where), except the measured inputs of (a), which become not compared. A bare new test in a file whose base copy binds nothing by computation and mentions the name nowhere stays set aside. The payload's shape; the report-only mode; the table's shape - a row may be reworded, none added without a reason.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the guard run on a diff: (a) both forms; a bare new test whose name the base copy holds inside a string; a new test in a class whose base body calls setattr on itself. Allow twins that must stay set aside: a bare new test in a file with no computed binding; a bare new test in ANOTHER class than the one whose body binds by computation; a string in the base copy that merely contains the name as part of a longer word. tasks.title: The config hold compares directories by identity, asks the tree a path is written in wherever it lies, and starts no process on an ordinary write
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the config hold follow what the loader would read found the measured hole closed, every earlier verdict unchanged, the errors handled and most of a wide table of arrangements right in both directions. It found four things in the guard's question; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator, the hook as a process, the write made, the loader asked.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A LINKED WORKTREE OUTSIDE THE PROJECT whose config folder is a symlink out of the repository: a session standing in the project writes that worktree's config, spelled through the link, config absent or present, by an edit tool or an MCP tool. Allowed, no journal row, and the loader asked for that worktree reads the written file. The tree a path lies in as written is taken as a candidate only when the path is spelled under the project. The documents say such a worktree's config is matched.
(b) A LETTER-CASE VARIANT ABOVE THE LINK'S DESTINATION: the project's config folder is a symlink; the write is spelled at the destination with a directory above it in another letter case, on a volume that folds case. Allowed, the loader reads the write - and the journal writes a config row for it, so the guard and the journal disagree. The same variant one component lower is held. The written path is matched against the resolved folder by its spelling.
(c) COST: a session standing in a linked worktree outside the project pays more git processes on every ordinary write than before that task - none before and some now for an edit in the project, and one more for an edit in that worktree - and tens of milliseconds with them, the same with no nested worktree and with many. The case that counts disk calls counts them with the session standing in the project and counts no process, so it cannot see this.
(d) THE PROPERTY CASE CANNOT FAIL when the candidate taken from the path as written is removed: every case stays green. An arrangement that needs it - a nested repository reached through a symlinked folder under the project - is held by the code and pinned by nothing.
Also measured, smaller: a linked worktree's config written at its link's outside destination is not held, which is outside the stated property, while the README's words read as if it were.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE SAME DIRECTORY IS DECIDED BY IDENTITY, NOT BY SPELLING. Wherever the question is whether the directory a write lands in is a candidate tree's config folder and both exist, it is answered by the two directories being one on disk. Spelling is read only below the nearest existing directory, by the per-directory rule on letter case that is already there.
2. THE TREE A PATH LIES IN AS WRITTEN is a candidate wherever the path lies - under the project or not - found from the path as spelled without resolving it.
3. AN ORDINARY WRITE STARTS NO PROCESS IT DID NOT START BEFORE THE HOLD FOLLOWED THE LOADER, from wherever the session stands, and lists no directory. Where the session's tree cannot be known without a process, it is found another way or asked only for a write that could be a config by what is already known; which, and why it loses no hold, is stated in the outcome.
4. THE PROPERTY CASE IS GENERATED, NOT LISTED: its arrangements are the product of named dimensions - whose config (the project's, the session's tree's, a linked worktree's outside the project, a nested worktree's, a nested repository's reached through a symlinked folder), the config folder (a real directory, a symlink inside, a symlink outside, a chain), the config present or absent, the spelling (through the link, at the destination, a letter-case variant at each directory level), where the session stands, the tool - with the impossible combinations named and skipped. For each it runs the hook, makes the write and asks the loader for the project, the session's tree and the tree as written; the verdict is a hold exactly when one of them reads the written file. The journal's agreement case runs over the same product.
5. THE DOCUMENTS say which trees are asked, and that a config written at a link's destination is held when one of those trees loads it and not otherwise.

WHAT STAYS. Every verdict and every word on every write of the earlier probes (the brief says where), except the measured inputs of (a) and (b), which become holds. The allow side: a file named like the config in a plain folder or in a symlinked folder that is no asked tree's config folder, a sibling of the config, a source file, a write outside every tree. The fail-mode table. The hook import budget.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the hook run as a process with the write made and the loader asked: (a) in its three forms; (b); the generated case red on the families of (a) and (b) before the change and green after. A case that counts processes as well as disk calls for an ordinary write with the session standing in the project, in a nested worktree and in a linked worktree outside it - no more than the tree before the hold followed the loader. Time per hook run before and after over thirty runs, twice with a gap, reported. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: identity put back to spelling; the as-written candidate dropped; the as-written candidate limited to under the project; the session's tree asked by a process on every write; and an allow row - every write spelled under any tree's config-named folder held - turns an allow twin red.

NOT in this task: the journal row for a config created through the shell or an MCP tool; a symlink FILE in the project pointing at an outside worktree's config; an exception of an unexpected kind inside the question, which stays the guard's fail-open row.

Acceptance:
(1) A linked worktree's config outside the project, its config folder a symlink, written through the link from a session standing in the project is refused for a subagent and asked of the main session, by an edit tool and by an MCP tool, config present or absent.
(2) A write spelled at a link's destination with a letter-case variant at any directory level is held where the loader then reads it, and the guard and the journal agree on it.
(3) An ordinary write starts no more processes than before the hold followed the loader from each of the three places a session stands, and lists no directory; the counts and the timing are reported before and after.
(4) The property case is generated from named dimensions, is red before on the measured families, and fails when the as-written candidate is removed.
(5) Every other verdict and word is unchanged and the allow twins are allowed.
(6) SECURITY.md, the README, the changelog and the build guide say which trees are asked and what a write at a link's destination gets, and are true of the code; the hook import budget gate is green.

tasks.title: A config created through the shell or an MCP tool leaves its journal row
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the config hold ran the route the documents call journalled and found the first write of it unrecorded. It was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator: the journal hook's two passes as processes around a real write.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands. No config exists - the default a project starts with. A shell command writes one, with the plan gate switched off; the journal hook runs before and after it. No row is written, and the loader then reads the switch as off. The same with the config folder a symlink, and the same for an MCP tool that creates the config - which the guard asks the main session about and the journal then does not record. With a config already present the row is written in every one of those forms. The pass after the write finds no record of the file as it stood before the call - there was no file - and takes that as nothing to compare with. SECURITY.md says the shell route is journalled.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. ABSENT IS A STATE THE PASS BEFORE THE CALL RECORDS. For each path the sweep records, the pass before a call notes that the file was absent, as it notes the bytes of one that is present. The pass after writes the row when the file exists and the note says it did not: a creation, said as one in the row's summary, with the state after.
2. THE SAME FOR EVERY PATH THE SWEEP RECORDS - the config, the plan's index and its phase files - since the same pass reads them all; a plan file created by a command is a row too, unless the trail already holds a row for that state, as today.
3. WITH THE JOURNAL SWITCHED OFF IN THE CONFIG THAT IS CREATED, the row is still written: the creation is the write that turned it off, as the flip of an existing config already is.
4. A PASS AFTER WITH NO PASS BEFORE - no note at all - writes nothing, as today: absence was not observed.

WHAT STAYS. Every row written today, byte for byte apart from time and chain fields. No row for a call that created nothing. The list of paths the sweep records - it is not widened. A row's shape and keys; a key may be added, none renamed or removed. The trail check's findings on every fixture of its suite.

HOW TO PROVE. The hook's two passes as processes around a real write in a real repository, red before: a shell redirect creating the config - a row; the same through a symlinked config folder; an MCP tool creating it - a row; a command creating a phase file - a row. Quiet twins: a command that creates nothing writes no row; a file absent before and absent after writes none; a file created and removed inside one call writes none; a pass after with no pass before writes none; a creation the trail already holds a row for is not written twice. One case that the trail check reads a creation row without a finding and anchors the next drift warning on it. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: absence not noted; the row withheld when the created config switches the journal off; and an allow row - a row whenever the file is present after - turns a quiet twin red.

NOT in this task: a file outside the sweep's list; a write of a nested tree's config through an MCP tool; reading the command's text to find what it wrote.

Acceptance:
(1) A config created by a shell command, also through a symlinked config folder, and by an MCP tool leaves a config row that says it was created.
(2) A plan file created by a command leaves its row unless the trail already records that state.
(3) A created config that switches the journal off still leaves its row.
(4) No row is written for a call that created nothing, for a file created and removed inside one call, or with no pass before.
(5) Every row written today is unchanged apart from time and chain fields, and the trail check reads a creation row without a finding.
(6) SECURITY.md, the README, the changelog and the build guide say what the shell and MCP routes leave in the journal, creation included, and are true of the code.

ADDED BEFORE START REPORTED BY THE EXECUTOR OF THE TASK BEFORE THIS ONE, TO BE MEASURED FIRST AND FIXED HERE IF IT REPRODUCES: with the hooks run as processes, the row for an existing config's journal switch going from on to off is computed and then not written - the append refuses it because the config on disk already says off - while the documents call that row the last one the journal writes. Rule 3 above meets the same refusal for a created config. So the rule covers both: the row for the write that switches the journal off, by an edit of an existing config or by creating one, is written when the hooks run as processes. Prove it red before with the hook's two passes as processes around an edit that flips the switch, and keep a quiet twin: with the journal already off before the call, a write of the config leaves no row. Acceptance (3) reads: a config write that switches the journal off, creating the file or editing it, still leaves its row when the hooks run as processes, and a write with the journal already off leaves none.

outcome.technical: (1) THE FLIP-ROW FAULT REPRODUCED. On HEAD code, cf5 (the journal hook as a process for both passes, rows read back from the trail) wrote no row for any of five writes that switch the journal off: a config created off by a command, by an MCP tool and by an edit tool, and an existing config flipped on->off by a command and by an edit tool (`python3 -B tests/test_journal_writes.py --selftest` before the fix: FAIL cf5 with rows [] for all five, exit codes [0, 0]). The refusal lives in _journal_io._append (`if not enabled(config): raise IOError("journal disabled ...")`), which the hook's _append_rows called with the config loaded from disk after the call. _journal_io.py is NOT changed: the Post pass now marks the row it owes because the switch was on before the call with a private entry key `_ON_BEFORE` (journal-writes.py, set in _swept_tree when the current switch is off, and on the edit lane only for a row whose target is CONFIG_REL); _append_rows pops that key and, only when the row goes into the project's own trail (_config._same_dir(troot, project)), hands append the loaded config with journal.enabled True. No other caller of append is touched; the key never reaches a row (_normalise builds the row from known fields, and post_entries strips it too). The slot is refreshed after the last will so the writer's next call does not owe it again (cq6). (2) ABSENT. `ABSENT = "absent"` is the slot's `sha256` value for a file that does not exist: _snapshot returns (ABSENT, None) on FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError and keeps (None, None) for any other OSError (unreadable). "No pass before" is no slot at all (_read_preimage returns None), told apart in _swept_tree: `pre is None` -> seed a present file, claim nothing (as before); `pre.sha256 == ABSENT` and the file present -> creation. cq3 shows both in one case: the same write with no Pre leaves [] and with a Pre leaves the creation row. A phase file's name is unknown before it exists, so the Pre pass keeps the shard directory's listing in a slot named `<shard dir>/` (_note_listing, written only when it changed; the listing is the one _swept_targets already made, now returned by the new _sweep_paths), and _absent_by_listing turns 'not in the noted listing' into an ABSENT note. (3) CREATION ROW: same keys as an edit row; no key added. Wording: summary `<tool> created <rel>` (_created_rows); a config created switched off appends `: journal.enabled true->false` with details.changes [the flip from the default]; a plan file gets details.reason CREATED_NOT_DERIVED and the same text in the summary, and no chained rows. The edit lane's rows keep their wording (`Write wrote ...`) byte for byte; the edit lane now also judges a created config's switch from the default, so a config an edit tool creates switched off leaves its flip row. verify/drift_anchor/newest_anchor read a creation row as an edit row: cc1 (test__journal_io) - creation row, verify ([], []), then an edit behind the journal warns exactly once naming .claude/audit.config.json. (4) Dedupe: an edit tool creating the config leaves exactly one row (cf6); a creation goes through the same recorded_states window check, so a verb's own row for the state is not repeated (cq4). (5) Orchestrator probes, copies under <SP>/sg1.47 (fixtures repointed there): probe_sh AFTER - real/linked x absent/plain/dest now each `[('config.edit', '.claude/audit.config.json')]` where BEFORE had [] (3 rows changed), every present row unchanged; probe_j - u20b changed DIS->ok (one config row), every other row's cfgrows identical to sg1.46-mine/probe_j.after.out; u21 STAYS DIS: it is an MCP write of a SIBLING linked worktree's config from a session standing in the project, and <SP>/sg1.47/w/probe_u21p.py shows no row before or after the change with that config ABSENT or PRESENT - the sweep does not read that tree's paths at all, which is the excluded 'another tree's config through an MCP tool' and would need the swept tree set widened; the documents now name it. twins.py WRONG: 0; probe_e identical to sg1.46-mine/probe_e.after.out (no warning, no finding); probe_a differing: 0 of 1960. (6) Mutation probe <SP>/sg1.47/mutations.py (output mutations.out), run from the worktree root on a copy: 11 rows, MUTATIONS ALL CAUGHT, exit 0 - absence snapshots as unreadable -> cf1 cf2 cf3 cf5 cq3 cc1; Pre does not note absence -> cf1 cf2 cf3 cf5 cq3; shard listing never kept -> cf4; created-off row withheld sweep lane -> cf5, edit lane -> cf5 cq6; flip row withheld (append handed the after config) -> cf5; last will twice, sweep lane slot -> cq6, edit lane slot -> cq6; ALLOW a row whenever the file is present after -> cq3 cq5 (also f10b f11 f5 f8 s1); ALLOW last will marked for any config row -> cq7; ALLOW creation written despite a verb's row -> cq4. (7) Runs, each exit 0 unless said: task gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --jobs 4 tests/test_journal_writes.py tests/test__journal_io.py` 2/2 files, 466 cases (184 + 282); dependants 7 suites 2319 cases: test_journal_writes 183, test__journal_io 282, test_audit_journal 186, test_hooks 247, test__config 413, test_drive_phase 1008, test_guard_edits FAILED once on cf32c only ('the disk image is detached again') - a file outside my scope, re-run alone 126/126; `python3 tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` exit 0 (3.14.7 only, other interpreters not measured); test__deps/test__output_lints/test__refs 3/3 files 792 cases; gate-parity.py 0; prove-gates.py --list 0; ruff and vermin clean on the changed .py files; run-test-gate.py SG1 --task SG1.47-ukq unrecorded: exit 0, 'GATE GREEN' (its affected/related suites included; tallies clipped by the tool without --verbose). An orphaned disk image from a guard-edits run (its scratch directory already gone) is still attached on this host; not detached by me. Suite seconds (sweep's own figures, --jobs 4): HEAD export test_journal_writes 29.9 s then 13.3 s, test__journal_io 19.8 s then 12.5 s (two runs with a gap; the first under load); this tree 16.4 s and 12.9 s. (8) Dependants: journal-writes.py stays registered Pre and Post in hooks.json unchanged; its readers test_journal_writes/test_hooks/test_audit_journal green; the existing oq6 comment that said the append refuses the flip was rewritten. _journal_io.py unchanged, so its importers (audit-journal, doctor, drive, panel journal views) and test__journal_io/test_audit_journal/test__doctor_policy read nothing new; no row key added, so COMPATIBILITY.md's row shape is untouched. tasks.title: The config hold asks every tree the repository registers, and its property case finds no tree by a walk of its own
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the config hold compare directories by identity and take the tree a path is written in as a candidate found a regression, the measured family still open in one form, and the property case unable to see either. Each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator: the hook as a process, the write made, the loader asked.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A REGRESSION. A nested worktree, or a repository reached through a symlinked folder under the project, whose config folder is a symlink to a directory that is itself a git repository: a subagent's write of that tree's config from a session standing in the project is allowed, by an edit tool and by an MCP tool, config absent or present; the tree's loader reads the write; and the journal row it had is gone. The tree before that task refused it. The walk that looks for the tree as written starts at the config folder; that folder holds a git entry, so the walk stops there and takes the folder as the tree. The candidate the earlier code asked - the directory the config's components hang off - was removed.
(b) THE SAME ROOT, NOT A REGRESSION. A linked worktree outside the project whose config folder is a symlink to a repository, or is itself a repository: written through that folder from a session standing in the project, allowed, and that worktree's loader reads it.
(c) THE PROPERTY CASE SHARES THE DEFECT. Its oracle finds the tree as written by a walk of its own with the same start and the same stop as the module's, so a tree whose config folder holds a git entry reaches neither. It is green on the tree as it stands and green on a copy with the walk's start corrected: it cannot tell the two apart. Its folder dimension has no value for a folder that holds or links to a repository.
(d) A DOCUMENT SENTENCE. The README says a config written at its link's destination is held when the destination lies in a tree of this repository. Measured: an outside linked worktree whose config folder links to a directory inside the project, the config written at that destination from a session in the project - allowed, and that worktree's loader reads it.
(e) Smaller, read and not run: the file that names a tree's common directory is opened without a check that it is a regular file.

This is the third round to find one more arrangement in which a tree that loads the written file was never asked. The trees are being found from the path's spelling; the rule below finds them from what the repository itself records.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. EVERY TREE THE REPOSITORY REGISTERS IS ASKED. For a write that could be a config by what is already known - its resolved last component is the config's name in any letter case, or the file is by identity an asked tree's existing config - the trees asked are the project, the tree the session stands in, the repository's main tree and every worktree the repository registers, read from the registrations in the repository's common directory without starting a process, wherever each lies and whatever its config folder is: a real directory, a symlink inside or outside, a chain, a directory that is itself a repository or holds a git entry. The write is held when for any of them the directory it lands in is that tree's config folder, by identity, and its name is the config's by that directory's rule on letter case - or the file is that tree's config by identity. A registration that names no existing directory is passed over.
2. A REPOSITORY NESTED UNDER THE PROJECT that is not a tree of this repository is asked by the directory the config's components hang off, as spelled and once resolved - the directory above the config folder, never the folder. A git entry inside a config folder decides nothing.
3. AN ORDINARY WRITE READS NO REGISTRATION, lists no directory and starts no process: the registrations are read only for a write rule 1 names. The files read to find a common directory and a registration are read only when regular files and to a bounded length.
4. THE PROPERTY CASE'S ORACLE OWES NOTHING TO THE MODULE. The fixture records every tree it builds; after the write the loader is asked for each of them; the verdict is a hold exactly when one reads the written file. The case finds no tree by a walk. Its folder dimension gains a symlink to a repository, a folder that is itself a repository and a folder holding an empty git entry; a destination dimension says whether a link's destination lies inside the project or outside. It fails when it ran none of a family. The journal's agreement case runs over the same product for the edit tools; an MCP write of another tree's config, which leaves no row today, is a skip it names.
5. THE DOCUMENTS state the property in one sentence - a write is held when a tree of this repository, or a repository nested under the project, would load the written file - and list what is still not matched from runs, not from the earlier list. A config written at a link's destination outside the project for a registered worktree becomes a hold; the sentences and the cases that say it is not matched change on purpose and are named in the outcome.

WHAT STAYS. The allow side, each as a twin: a file named like the config in a plain folder that is no tree's config folder; a config-named file under a directory holding a stray git entry that is no repository; the config of an unrelated repository outside the project that this repository does not register; a sibling of the config; a source file; a write outside every tree. Every verdict and word of the earlier probes on writes rule 1 and rule 2 do not name (the brief says where). The process counts and the absence of a listing on an ordinary write from each place a session stands. The fail-mode table. The hook import budget.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the hook run as a process with the write made and the loader asked: (a) in both families; (b) in both forms; (d); the generated case red on the tree as it stands once its oracle is independent, and green after. A case that counts processes, listings and registration reads for an ordinary write - none - and shows the registrations are read for a config-named write. A stale registration, a registration that is a directory or a pipe, and a common-directory file that is no regular file each leave the verdict standing and raise nothing. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the walk's start put back to the config folder; the registrations not read; the registrations read on every write; the main tree left out; the oracle's trees taken from the module instead of the fixture - which must be shown to make the case blind, by the case staying green over a broken module; and an allow row - every config-named write under any directory holding a git entry held - turns an allow twin red.

NOT in this task: the journal row for an MCP write of another tree's config; a write through the shell; a symlink FILE in the project pointing at another tree's config; a repository nested under a tree other than the project.

Acceptance:
(1) A nested worktree's or a nested repository's config whose config folder is a symlink to a repository is refused for a subagent and asked of the main session, by an edit tool and an MCP tool, config present or absent, and its journal row is written again.
(2) An outside linked worktree's config whose config folder is or links to a repository, and one written at a link's destination inside or outside the project, is held from a session standing in the project.
(3) An ordinary write reads no registration, lists no directory and starts no process from each place a session stands; a stale or malformed registration changes no verdict and raises nothing.
(4) The property case asks the loader for every tree its fixture built, finds none by a walk, covers the new folder and destination values, and fails when the walk's start is put back.

tasks.title: The row for the write that switched the journal off is owed only by the call whose own pass before read the switch as on
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the journal record a created file and the write that switches the journal off found the creation half right in every state it drove, and a regression in the other half. It was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator: the journal hook's passes as processes around real writes in a real repository, then the trail check.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands, each with no such row on the tree before that task.
(a) THE JOURNAL IS SWITCHED OFF BY SOMEONE ELSE, AND A CALL THAT WROTE NOTHING GETS THE ROW. The owner switches the journal off by hand, or through the panel, or creates a config that has it off; the session's next command - one that lists a directory - leaves a row saying the journal went from on to off, credited to that session. The same when another session switched it off: the second session's next command adds a second row. The same for every subagent of the session that ever ran a command: each adds one, under its own agent name. The same when the next call is an MCP read.
(b) THE TRAIL CHECK IS SILENCED BY IT. The owner switches the journal off by hand and an edit tool then rewrites the config: the extra row credits that write with the flip, and the trail check, which warned about an edit the journal never saw, no longer warns.
Every such row is valid in the chain and raises no finding. The pass before a call returns before it notes anything while the journal is off, so the note a writer holds is the one its earlier call left, from when the switch was on; the pass after reads that note as the state before this call, and the append now accepts the row.
(c) THE RULE THAT THIS ROW GOES ONLY INTO THE PROJECT'S OWN TRAIL IS HELD BY NO CASE. With the check that says so removed, every case stays green; the case the documents cite for it writes through the other lane and never reaches the check. On a linked worktree outside the project with the project's journal off, removing the check puts a row into that worktree's trail.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE SWITCH AS IT STOOD BEFORE THE CALL IS WHAT THIS CALL'S OWN PASS BEFORE READ. A row is marked as the write that switched the journal off only when the pass before of the same call - the same tool call id - read the switch as on, or found no config, and the pass after reads it off. A note left by an earlier call, by another session or by another agent is not that reading. A call with no pass before, or whose payload names no call id, marks nothing.
2. WITH THE SWITCH OFF BEFORE THE CALL NOTHING IS WRITTEN, by the sweep or by the edit lane, whatever notes exist from earlier calls: none of the measured inputs leaves a row beyond the flip's own, and the trail check warns again about the hand edit of (b).
3. TWO CALLS IN FLIGHT ACROSS THE FLIP each owe their row when each read the switch as on before and reads it off after; the one that cannot tell whose write it was says so and names no session, as today.
4. THE ROW GOES INTO THE PROJECT'S OWN TRAIL AND ONLY FOR THAT TRAIL'S OWN CONFIG, and a case fails when that check is removed - on the lane where the check is reached.
5. THE DOCUMENTS say whose row the last one is - the call that switched the journal off, by its own reading before and after - and cite for each rule a case that fails without it.

WHAT STAYS. Every row written with the journal on, byte for byte apart from time and chain fields. The row for a write that switches the journal off by a command, an MCP tool or an edit tool, creating the config or editing it, written once and not again by the next call. No row with the journal already off before the call. The creation rows and their quiet twins. The trail check's findings and warnings on every fixture of its suite. No new process and no new directory listing on either pass; with the journal off the pass before does no more than it must to satisfy rule 1, and what that is - and why it is not the plugin working after being told to stop - is stated in the outcome.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the hook's passes as processes with a note that predates the switch - a writer that made an earlier call while the journal was on: the owner's hand flip followed by a command, by an MCP read and by an edit-tool rewrite of the config; another session's flip followed by this session's command; a subagent's command after its session's flip; a config created switched off by hand followed by a command. Each leaves no row beyond the flip's own, and the trail check warns where a hand edit went unrecorded. The cases start from a writer with an earlier call, never from a fresh fixture. A case for rule 3 with the two calls' passes interleaved. A case for rule 4 on a linked worktree outside the project. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the mark taken from whatever note exists; the mark given without the call id matching; the project-trail check removed; and an allow row - the mark never given - turns the flip's own row red.

NOT in this task: a stale note that says a file was absent when an owner created it by hand between calls whose pass before never ran; the journal row for an MCP write of another tree's config; the cost of the pass before on a plan with hundreds of phase files.

Acceptance:
(1) After the journal is switched off by hand, through the panel, by another session or by creating a config that has it off, a later call that did not switch it off leaves no row - a command, an MCP read, an edit-tool write, by the session or by a subagent.
(2) The trail check warns about a config edited by hand to switch the journal off also after an edit tool rewrites that config.
(3) The call that switches the journal off, by any tool, creating the config or editing it, still leaves its one row, and two calls in flight across the flip each leave theirs.
(4) The row is written only into the project's own trail for that trail's own config, and a case fails when the check is removed.
(5) Every row written with the journal on is unchanged apart from time and chain fields, and neither pass starts a process or lists a directory it did not before.
(6) SECURITY.md, the README, the changelog and the build guide say whose row the last one is and cite cases that hold each rule, and are true of the code.

tasks.title: The floor guard knows a skip or a mark by one table, reads a class with its same-file bases and a namespace handed to a same-file helper, and every row of its binding tables carries the example that holds it
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that stopped a bare new test being set aside where the base copy can have bound its name found the two measured inputs answered, the five surviving widenings now red, no honest suite of this repository made noisier and the documents' sentences on labels true. It found four things; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A REGRESSION, NOISY. A class decorated with a skip or a mark spelled bare - skipIf or skipUnless imported from unittest by name, mark imported from pytest by name - and given one honest new test: the file read clean before that task and is now not compared, with the reason that the class binds names by computation through a class decorator. The module holds two lists of what a skip or a mark is: the one that sets a skip's reason aside knows the bare spellings, the one that decides a decorator only marks knows the dotted ones alone. The suite's own case uses the dotted list too and cannot see it.
(b) UNSAFE, NOT A REGRESSION. Tests generated into a same-file base class or mixin - by a store into what locals hands out in the mixin's body, or by setattr on the base from module level - and a subclass given a bare test under a generated name: clean, and run side by side the base copy has a failing test the tree copy lacks. The class a test lands in is read alone; its same-file bases are followed only for a subclass hook or a metaclass. The task left out bases from another module, not these.
(c) UNSAFE, NOT A REGRESSION. A helper defined in the same file is handed what globals or locals returns and stores the generated tests into it: clean, and a failing test is lost the same way. The reason the task gave for not reading a namespace handed to a call - the callee may only read it - is true of a runner in another module and false of a helper whose body is in the file.
(d) READINGS THE SUITE DOES NOT HOLD. With any one of these removed from the module every case stays green, and for each an input exists that the module as it stands reads not compared and the changed module reads clean: a write through the namespace by update or setdefault; eval as a form; vars of the module taken through sys.modules; a base with a metaclass as a hook; hooks followed through further bases; a decorator that is a call read as marking only; a nested class's scope read as its outermost class. The suite's own oracle agrees with the module only on the one form in its fixture.
Also measured, smaller: the README's list of forms omits two the tables hold.

WHAT WAS MEASURED BEFORE WRITING THIS RULE, so that it is not tried again. Reading the whole file for the mere presence of a means of binding - setattr, a namespace's dictionary, exec, the modules table - with the harmless uses named, convicts the largest and most edited suites of this repository, because they patch the module under test by setattr: the orchestrator's scan flags a tenth of the test files, the biggest among them. So the reading stays by scope and by form; this task makes each form a row that cannot stand unheld and says in the documents, in one place, what is not read.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. ONE TABLE SAYS WHAT A SKIP OR A MARK IS. The reading that sets a skip's reason aside and the reading that decides a decorator only marks ask the same table, with the same spellings - dotted and bare - and a spelling added to one is added to both by construction. A class decorator the table knows binds nothing; the measured shapes of (a) read clean again.
2. A CLASS IS READ WITH ITS SAME-FILE BASES. The scope a method lands in is its class and every base of it defined in the same file, through further bases: a form that binds by computation in any of them, and a setattr on any of them from anywhere in the module, binds for the subclass. A base from another module stays unread.
3. A NAMESPACE HANDED TO A CALLEE THIS FILE DEFINES IS A BINDING of the scope whose namespace it is; handed to a callee the file does not define it is not, as today. A callee is defined by the file when the file holds a function, class, lambda assignment or method of that name at any depth; a name the file binds only by an import is not.
4. EVERY ROW OF THE BINDING TABLES CARRIES ITS OWN EXAMPLE - a base copy and the new test that must then be not compared - and one case runs every row's example against the module and against the module with that row removed: the example reads not compared with the row and clean without it. A row with no example, or whose example reads the same without it, fails the case; so a reading cannot be in the module and unheld. A row that is equivalent to another is removed, not kept. The suite's own oracle for the bare-new-test row is checked against the same examples.
5. THE DOCUMENTS LIST EVERY FORM THE TABLES HOLD, BY THE TABLES' OWN NAMES, AND IN ONE PLACE WHAT IS NOT READ: a namespace handed to a callee in another module; a base class from another module; a module reached through an alias; a descriptor's naming hook; a module-level attribute hook; a name bound by another module at import. They say the row is a reading of forms and that a test bound in a way the tables do not hold is not seen.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer on every input of the earlier probes and of the orchestrator's inputs (the brief says where), except the shapes of (a), which read clean again, and the inputs of (b) and (c), which become not compared. A bare new test in every test file of this repository reads as it reads today - none of them flips. The dotted decorators stay clean. The payload's shape; the report-only mode; the table of what is set aside - no row added.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the guard run on a diff: the shapes of (a) not compared; the inputs of (b) and (c) clean, each also executed to show the failing test lost; the row case red for each reading of (d). Allow twins that must stay set aside: a class with a dotted skip, a class with a bare skip, a subclass of a same-file base that binds nothing by computation, a namespace handed to an imported runner, a helper defined in the file that is handed something else than a namespace. A bare new test appended to every test file of this repository, before and after: no file flips, the count reported. The measurement over this repository's task commits before and after, every changed commit judged from its diff. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: each table row removed - held by the row case by construction, shown for every row; the two skip readings given separate tables again; the same-file bases not followed; the handed namespace not read; and allow rows - every class decorator binding, every base binding whichever file defines it, a namespace handed to any callee binding - each turn a twin red.

NOT in this task: any form listed as not read under rule 5; a docstring holding an example that stops being a docstring; whether the guard is labelled experimental.

Acceptance:
(1) A class decorated with a skip or a mark in a bare spelling and given a bare new test reads clean, and the two readings of what a skip or a mark is ask one table.
(2) A bare new test under a name generated into a same-file base or mixin, or stored by a same-file helper handed the namespace, is not compared, and the measured inputs no longer read clean.
(3) Every row of the binding tables carries an example, and the case fails for a row with none or one whose example reads the same without the row.
(4) Every allow twin is set aside, and a bare new test appended to each test file of this repository reads as before.
(5) The measurement over the repository's task commits is reported before and after, every changed answer judged from its diff.
(6) The README, the build guide and the changelog list the forms by the tables' names and in one place what is not read, and are true of the code.

tasks.title: A call's own reading of the journal switch is kept per call, so a second call of the same writer cannot take the switch-off row away, and the documents say whose row a switch-off in an open call's window is
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the switch-off row owed only by the call whose own pass before read the switch as on found the false rows gone, the rows written with the journal on unchanged byte for byte apart from time and chain fields, and the guard that reads the same start record unmoved. It found two things; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A REGRESSION. The reading is per call, and it is stored in the one start record a writer has. Two calls of ONE writer in flight: the second call's pass before replaces the record, the first call's pass after finds a record naming another call and marks nothing. Order - the flipping call's pass before, a second call's pass before, the second's pass after, the flip, the flipping call's pass after: no row, and the trail check says nothing, so the switch-off leaves no record anywhere; the tree before that task wrote the row. The same with an MCP write and an MCP read. With the second call's pass after last, the one row comes from the second call. The suite's case for two calls in flight drives two sessions only, and the documents say two calls in flight across the flip each leave theirs.
(b) A SENTENCE THAT IS FALSE. The README says a switch turned off by hand or in the panel leaves no row at all. Flipped by hand, or through the panel's own write, WHILE one ordinary call is open - a session's test run, a subagent's MCP read - that call's pass after writes the row under its own session and agent: its own pass before read on, its pass after reads off, and no peer is in the window, since neither a hand edit nor the panel leaves one. Between calls there is no row, as the sentence says. The behaviour is the sweep's and older than that task; the absolute sentence is new.
(c) NOT DRIVEN, READ FROM THE HOST'S DOCUMENTATION. The host documents that the pass after runs for a tool call that succeeded and that a call that failed - a command exiting non-zero included - is reported under another event, which this plugin does not register. If so, a switch-off made by a command that then fails has no pass after and leaves no row; before that task the next call wrote it. Registering that event is a task of its own in the next phase; here the documents must not claim more than is built.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE READING IS KEPT PER CALL. What a pass before read of the switch is stored under that call's own id, where no other call's pass before can replace it, and the pass after reads its own and no other. The start record the Bash-write guard reads keeps the shape and the meaning it has; say whether it still carries the reading and who reads it.
2. EVERY CALL IN WHOSE WINDOW THE FLIP LANDED LEAVES ITS ROW, THE SAME WRITER'S INCLUDED - which is what the documents already say. So: the order of (a) writes the flipping call's row; with both calls open across the flip each leaves one; a call whose window closed before the flip leaves none; a call that began after the flip leaves none, as today.
3. NOTHING NEW IS LEFT BEHIND. With the switch off before a call, its pass before stores no reading - absence already means no mark. A reading is removed by its own pass after. One left by a call whose pass after never ran is removed by a stated rule that is bounded and does not depend on that call ever returning; say which, and what it costs an ordinary call. Two passes before of one writer running at the same moment must not lose either reading - a read-modify-write of one shared file is not that.
4. THE DOCUMENTS SAY WHOSE ROW IT IS, IN ONE PLACE. A switch-off by hand or in the panel between calls leaves no row and the trail check does not see it. One that lands while a call is open is recorded under that call, as any write the sweep sees in a call's window is: the row says in whose window the switch went off, not whose hand did it. A switch-off by a call whose pass after never runs leaves no row. Each of the three is cited to a case that shows it.

WHAT STAYS. Every row written with the journal on, byte for byte apart from time and chain fields. Every answer of the orchestrator's ten inputs and of the earlier rounds' probes (the brief says where), except the orders of (a), which gain their row. The false rows the last task removed stay removed: a later call after someone else's switch-off writes nothing. The Bash-write guard's verdicts. The hook import budget.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the hook's passes run as processes around a real write in a real repository: the order of (a) by a command and by an MCP tool - no row; both calls open across the flip - one row where two are owed. Allow twins that must stay quiet: a second call of the same writer that began after the flip; one whose window closed before it; a hand flip between calls; a call with no call id. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the reading stored per writer again; the pass after reading any call's reading; a reading stored with the switch off; a reading never removed; the leftover rule removed - each red on a named case; and allow rows - every call after the flip marked, no call marked - each turn a twin red.

NOT in this task: registering the host's event for a failed call; who is named when a hand edit lands in an open call's window, beyond saying so; an MCP write of another tree's config.

Acceptance:
(1) With two calls of one writer in flight, the call that switched the journal off leaves its row whatever the order of the other call's passes, shown by a command and by an MCP tool.
(2) A call that began after the flip, or whose window closed before it, leaves no row, and a call with no call id marks nothing.
(3) No reading is stored while the switch is off, a reading is removed by its own pass after, and one whose pass after never ran is removed by the stated bounded rule.
(4) Every row written with the journal on is unchanged apart from time and chain fields, and the Bash-write guard's verdicts are unchanged.
(5) SECURITY.md, the README, the build guide and the changelog say whose row a switch-off between calls, in an open call's window and by a call with no pass after is, each cited to a case, and are true of the code.

tasks.title: The config hold finds the repository from the checkout the project lies in, asks each registered tree at the project's own place in it, and a registration written relative is held by a case
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that made the config hold ask every tree the repository registers found no regression: every form of registration git writes - plain, relative, moved, locked, the project itself a linked worktree, a bare repository, a separate git directory, a worktree of a submodule - went from allowed to held and matches the loader; malformed registrations raise nothing; a hundred worktrees cost an ordinary write nothing; the journal rows follow the guard. It found two things; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) THE RULE IS NOT BUILT FOR A MEMBER PROJECT. The registrations are found from the project's own git entry. A project that is a subdirectory of its checkout - the member-project arrangement this module names itself - has none, so no registration is read and neither the checkout's top nor any worktree is asked. With the checkout R, a worktree W and the project R/app, `git worktree list` from the project prints both; all four of these are allowed for a subagent and for the main session while a loader reads the write: W's config folder a link, written through it; the same written at its destination; R's config folder a link, written at its destination; and the member's own place in the worktree, W/app, written directly. The tree before that task allowed the same, so this is not a regression; the README's 'every registered worktree's' and SECURITY.md's passage say more than is built.
(b) A READING NO CASE HOLDS. Dropping the join of a relative registration with its own directory leaves the guard suite and the journal suite green; no fixture writes a registration relative. With one, the tree as it stands holds the write and the changed module allows it while the loader reads it.
Also measured, smaller: the comment beside the pointer bound says a cut pointer names nothing, and a cut line of slashes and letters resolves to the root, which is then asked as a tree - one tree too many, never a write let through; and the documents list a worktree whose registration is gone as not matched while one under the project is held - more than is claimed.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE REPOSITORY IS THE ONE THE PROJECT LIES IN. For a config-named write the common directory is found from the first directory at or above the project that holds a git entry - by lstat, bounded, no process, no listing - not from the project's own entry alone. An ordinary write still walks nothing it does not walk today.
2. A TREE IS ASKED WHERE A SESSION WOULD OPEN IT. When the project lies below its checkout's top by a relative path, each registered tree and the main tree is asked at its top and at that same relative place below it - the member's place in that tree - since either can be the directory a loader is handed. For a project that is its checkout's top the two are one and nothing changes.
3. THE PROPERTY CASE GAINS THE MEMBER DIMENSION, and its fixture records every place it built that a loader could be handed - each tree's top and each member place - so the oracle still owes nothing to the module. A registration written relative is a row of the same fixture, by the means git itself offers where the installed git has it and by a stated other means where not; say which and why it holds on the continuous-integration runners.
4. A POINTER CUT AT THE BOUND IS PASSED OVER, so the comment is true. The documents say what is matched and what is not from runs: the member project's trees are matched; a registration that is gone is listed by where it is held and where it is not.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer of every earlier probe and of the reviewer's regression matrix (the brief says where), except the four rows of (a), which become holds, each with its journal row for an edit tool. Ordinary writes: no registration read, no listing, no process, the disk-call case unchanged for them. The journal's answers. The hook import budget.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the guard run as a process on a real repository with a real worktree: the four rows of (a) allowed while the loader reads the write; the relative-registration row green over the changed module. Allow twins that must stay quiet: an ordinary write in a member project and in its worktree; a config-named file in a member project's tree that no place a loader is handed reads; a project that is its checkout's top, unchanged. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the common directory taken from the project's own entry again; the member place not asked; the relative join dropped; a cut pointer read; and allow rows - every directory above the project asked as a tree, every subdirectory of a registered tree asked - each turn a twin red.

NOT in this task: a folder beside an empty git entry that is no repository being held; a repository outside the project that is not this one; writes through the shell; an MCP write of another tree's config leaving no journal row.

Acceptance:
(1) In a member project, a config-named write that the checkout's top, a registered worktree, or the member's place in either would load is blocked for a subagent and asked about for the main session, and leaves its journal row for an edit tool.
(2) An ordinary write in a member project reads no registration, lists nothing and starts no process, and a project that is its checkout's top answers as before.
(3) The generated case covers the member dimension with trees taken from its fixture, and a registration written relative is held by a case that goes red when the join is dropped.
(4) A pointer cut at the bound asks no tree, and SECURITY.md, the README, the build guide and the changelog say what is matched and what is not, true of the code.

tasks.title: The documents say when the trail check sees a switch-off made by hand between calls, and a case holds that an ordinary call leaves no reading behind
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that keeps a call's reading of the journal switch per call found no regression: no row re-reports another call's change, three calls open across the flip each leave a row, a call that began after it leaves none, a pass after run twice leaves one, names of readings and of preimage slots cannot collide, and an ordinary call lists nothing and starts no process. It found two things; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A SENTENCE THAT IS FALSE, in four documents. SECURITY.md, the README, the build guide and the changelog say that when the switch is turned off by hand or in the panel between calls there is no row and the trail check does not see it, citing a case. That case deletes the journal before the hand flip, so no row records the config and the check has nothing to compare. With a row that records the config - a panel save, an edit-tool or a command write made while the journal was on, which is the ordinary state - a hand flip between calls draws the check's warning that the config has changed since the last row that recorded it, with or without a later call. The code did not change; the sentence was written into that task's own rule by the orchestrator from a run on an empty journal, and replaced a true one.
(b) A REMOVAL NO CASE HOLDS AT ITS CALL SITE. With the pass after changed to remove its reading only when it marks a flip, the journal suite stays green, and every ordinary command, MCP or subagent call made with the journal on then leaves its reading in the state directory until the age sweep. The case that holds the removal drives the helper alone.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE SENTENCE SAYS WHAT A RUN SHOWS, in each of the four documents and in one wording: a switch-off by hand or in the panel between calls leaves no row; the trail check warns that the config has changed since the last row that recorded it whenever such a row exists, and is silent only when no row ever recorded the config. It cites one case for each half, and the case for the first half has a row that records the config before the flip.
2. AN ORDINARY CALL LEAVES NO READING, HELD WHERE IT IS REMOVED: after an ordinary call with the journal on - by a command, by an MCP tool, by a subagent - through the hook's passes run as processes, the state directory holds no reading of that call; and after the pass before alone it holds exactly one, so the case cannot pass by the reading never having been written.

WHAT STAYS. No file under the plugin's hooks or scripts changes. Every other sentence of the passage, and every case as it is, apart from the one the sentence cites if it must gain its row.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before: the new case for the sentence's first half fails on the documents' present wording only by reading - so show it by the run: a config row, a hand flip between calls, the check's warning text; and the same on an empty journal, silent. tasks.title: The documents say when the trail check sees a switch-off made by hand between calls, and a case holds that an ordinary call leaves no reading behind
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that keeps a call's reading of the journal switch per call found no regression: no row re-reports another call's change, three calls open across the flip each leave a row, a call that began after it leaves none, a pass after run twice leaves one, names of readings and of preimage slots cannot collide, and an ordinary call lists nothing and starts no process. It found two things; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A SENTENCE THAT IS FALSE, in four documents. SECURITY.md, the README, the build guide and the changelog say that when the switch is turned off by hand or in the panel between calls there is no row and the trail check does not see it, citing a case. That case deletes the journal before the hand flip, so no row records the config and the check has nothing to compare. With a row that records the config - a panel save, an edit-tool or a command write made while the journal was on, which is the ordinary state - a hand flip between calls draws the check's warning that the config has changed since the last row that recorded it, with or without a later call. The code did not change; the sentence was written into that task's own rule by the orchestrator from a run on an empty journal, and replaced a true one.
(b) A REMOVAL NO CASE HOLDS AT ITS CALL SITE. With the pass after changed to remove its reading only when it marks a flip, the journal suite stays green, and every ordinary command, MCP or subagent call made with the journal on then leaves its reading in the state directory until the age sweep. The case that holds the removal drives the helper alone.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE SENTENCE SAYS WHAT A RUN SHOWS, in each of the four documents and in one wording: a switch-off by hand or in the panel between calls leaves no row; the trail check warns that the config has changed since the last row that recorded it whenever such a row exists, and is silent only when no row ever recorded the config. It cites one case for each half, and the case for the first half has a row that records the config before the flip.
2. AN ORDINARY CALL LEAVES NO READING, HELD WHERE IT IS REMOVED: after an ordinary call with the journal on - by a command, by an MCP tool, by a subagent - through the hook's passes run as processes, the state directory holds no reading of that call; and after the pass before alone it holds exactly one, so the case cannot pass by the reading never having been written.

WHAT STAYS. No file under the plugin's hooks or scripts changes. Every other sentence of the passage, and every case as it is, apart from the one the sentence cites if it must gain its row.

HOW TO PROVE. Both cases pin behaviour that is already right, so they pass on the tree before this task: the proof is green on the base, and that each can fail is shown by mutation, on a copy and never on this checkout. For rule 1: a config row, a hand flip between calls, the check's warning; the same on an empty journal, silent; red when the check is made silent, and red when it is made to warn on the empty journal. For rule 2: the reviewer's mutation of the call site - the suite green without your case and red with it. Allow twin: a call whose pass after never ran leaves its one reading, as the documents already say.

NOT in this task: any change to the hook; a config write that moves the state directory; a payload with no call id.

Acceptance:
(1) SECURITY.md, the README, the build guide and the changelog say that a switch-off by hand between calls leaves no row and that the trail check warns whenever a row recorded the config, each half cited to a case that shows it.
(2) A case run through the hook's passes fails when the pass after keeps the reading of an ordinary call, for a command, an MCP tool and a subagent, and requires the reading to exist between the two passes.
