tasks.title: The checkout the walk finds is itself asked, a git entry that is no repository does not end the walk, and the member path is held at more than one directory
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that built the config hold for a member project found no regression: a project whose checkout is a linked worktree, a member three directories down through a symlinked parent, a project spelled in another letter case, ordinary writes in every place, the regression matrix and the generated case's oracle all came out right. It found two things and one smaller; each was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) THE CHECKOUT THE WALK FINDS IS NOT ASKED when its common directory is not named for a plain repository. The walk finds the directory above the project that holds the git entry, and that directory is used only to find the common directory; the main tree is added only when the common directory's last name is the plain one. So in a member project of a repository made with a separate git directory, and of a project inside a submodule, the checkout's own top - which git itself prints as the toplevel - is never asked: its config written at its linked-out folder's destination is allowed for a subagent and for the main session while that top's loader reads it. The tree before that task allowed the same; the README, SECURITY.md and the build guide say the checkout top's config is matched for a project below it.
(b) THE MEMBER PATH IS HELD AT ONE DIRECTORY ONLY. Every member fixture puts the project one directory below its checkout. With the member path cut to its last component, or with the walk stopped one directory above the project, the guard's member, generated and registration cases and the journal's generated case stay green, and at two directories each change allows a write its loader reads. The code as it stands is right at two and three; no case says so.
(c) SMALLER, the same walk. A git entry that is no repository - an empty directory - between a member project and its real checkout ends the walk there, while git passes over it and prints the real checkout: the checkout top's config, a worktree's, and the member's place in the worktree are then allowed while read. Allowed before that task too.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. THE DIRECTORY THE WALK FINDS IS A TREE AND IS ASKED, at its top and at the member's place, whatever its common directory is named and whether or not any registration exists. The main-tree reading by the common directory's name stays for what it adds - the main tree of a project that is a linked worktree.
2. THE WALK ENDS AT A REPOSITORY, NOT AT A NAME. A git entry ends it when it is a directory holding a HEAD entry or a regular file whose first line, read to a bound, names a git directory; any other entry of that name is passed over and the walk goes on. By lstat and one bounded read, no listing, no process, and still only for a config-named write.
3. THE MEMBER DIMENSION OF THE FIXTURES HAS A PROJECT MORE THAN ONE DIRECTORY BELOW ITS CHECKOUT, in the measured rows and in the generated case, so the two changes of (b) each turn a named case red.
4. THE DOCUMENTS say what is matched from runs: the checkout top for a member project of a separate-git-directory repository and of a submodule moves to matched; the not-matched item on a separate git directory keeps only what a run still shows allowed.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer of every earlier probe and of the reviewer's regression runs (the brief says where), except the rows of (a) and (c), which become holds, each with its journal row for an edit tool. Ordinary writes: no walk, no registration read, no listing, no process. A project that is its checkout's top answers as before, and its config-named write makes the calls it makes today plus what rule 2's test of the project's own entry adds - measured, in the disk-call case. The journal's answers. The hook import budget.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the guard run as a process on real repositories: the two rows of (a) and the three of (c) allowed while a loader reads the write; the two changes of (b) green over the suites. Allow twins that must stay quiet: an ordinary write in each of those arrangements; a config-named file in a member project that no place a loader is handed reads; a directory holding an empty git entry and nothing above it that is a repository - no tree found, nothing asked beyond today. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the found top not asked; the walk ended at any entry of the name; the member path cut to its last component; the walk stopped one directory above the project; and an allow row - every directory the walk passes asked as a tree - turns a twin red.

NOT in this task: a config-named write beside an empty git entry being held by the nested-repository reading; anything on the documents' not-matched list other than the separate-git-directory item; writes through the shell.

Acceptance:
(1) In a member project of a repository with a separate git directory and of a project inside a submodule, a config-named write the checkout's top would load is blocked for a subagent and asked about for the main session, and leaves its journal row for an edit tool.
(2) A git entry that is no repository between a member project and its checkout does not end the walk, and the three measured rows are held.
(3) A member project two directories below its checkout is held by cases that go red when the member path is cut or the walk stops early.
(4) An ordinary write walks nothing and reads no registration, and a project that is its checkout's top answers as before.
(5) SECURITY.md, the README, the build guide and the changelog say what is matched and what is not, true of the code.

tasks.title: The floor guard sets a bare new test aside only on proof: a name is its import when the file binds it once, a base and a namespace are followed or declined, and a generated case executes both copies to hold it
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that gave the floor guard one table of skip and mark forms, same-file bases and same-file callees found two inputs that read clean now and read not compared before, each losing a failing test when run, and showed that the reading is still a list of the ways a name can be bound, checked by examples of one spelling each. Every item below was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator, both copies executed.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) REGRESSION, a failing test lost and read clean. A bare skip name the file imports and then rebinds by assignment to a decorator that generates tests; and a bare skip name that reaches the module through a star import while its import from unittest stands only inside a function that is never called. Both read not compared before that task. The import reading walks the whole file and takes only a function or class definition as taking a name away from its import.
(b) The same class, clean before and after: the module name itself rebound by assignment and a skip then spelled through it; a generating same-file class reached as a base through an alias assignment or returned by a same-file factory; a same-file callee reached through a rename; the namespace handed inside a list, through a partial, or as the function itself, not called. Each loses a failing test.
(c) REGRESSION on honest input: with the test module imported from two places in one try statement, a class carrying a dotted skip and given an honest new test reads not compared where it read clean, and a changed skip REASON on a method reads as a finding - a changed head - where the reason was set aside.
(d) CHECKS THAT CANNOT FAIL. Eight changes of the module leave the suite green and each makes an input lose a failing test or an honest input stop reading clean: a lambda no longer a callee; a method no longer a callee; a class no longer a callee; a namespace handed by keyword not read; only the first base followed; an aliased module import keyed by the module's own name; a name imported from two places read as written; a relative import's level dropped. The case that holds every table row takes the row out, but every example uses one spelling: a function callee by bare name, a positional argument, a first base.
(e) The guide says the ways left unread stand in one paragraph and nowhere else; the alias, the factory and the rename of (b) are not in it.

THE RULE TO BUILD. The reading stops listing the ways a name can be bound and asks for proof that it is not: a bare new test is set aside only where everything the reading leans on is proven, and whatever is not proven reads not compared - never clean, never a finding.
1. ONE RESOLUTION OF A NAME. A name stands for an import only when the file binds that name exactly once, by any means at any depth - an import, an assignment of any kind, a loop or with or except target, a definition, a parameter, a global declaration, a comprehension - and that one binding is an import at module level; a star import anywhere in the file proves no bare name. A dotted spelling is resolved through its first name the same way. Every reading that asks what a name is - a skip or mark form, a base, a callee - asks this one function.
2. A NAME THAT DOES NOT RESOLVE IS NEVER A FINDING. Where a decorator or call is spelled as a skip or mark form and its name does not resolve, the class or test it stands on reads not compared, with a reason naming the name and how it is bound; a changed reason there is not reported as a changed head.
3. A BASE IS FOLLOWED OR DECLINED. Each base of a class given a bare new test is one of: a name that resolves to a module-level import (another module's, unread, as documented); a bare name the file binds once, by a class statement (followed, through its own bases, wherever it stands among the bases); anything else - an alias, a call, a subscript, a name bound more than once anywhere in the file - not compared, with a reason true of the file as a whole.
4. A NAMESPACE THAT ESCAPES IS A BINDING. A reference to the file's own namespace - globals, locals, vars with no argument, called or not - is proven harmless only where it is read in place (subscripted to load, tested for membership, iterated, asked through a reading method) or handed, by position or keyword and directly, to a callee proven to be another module's or a builtin that writes nothing. Any other use - bound to a name, placed in a container, handed to a callee that is not proven, returned - reads not compared. The staged suites of this repository hand globals() to an imported runner and must stay clean.
5. THE CASE THAT HOLDS IT EXECUTES. One generated case builds pairs of copies from the dimensions the rule names - each way of binding the tables hold; each kind of callee (function, lambda, method, static method, class, nested function, renamed, through a partial); each way of handing (position, keyword, inside a container, uncalled); each place and spelling of a base (first, later, through two levels, alias, factory); each spelling of a skip or mark (dotted, bare with its import, aliased module, rebound, shadowed in another scope, star import, import inside a function, imported from two places) - together with the honest twin of each, and RUNS both copies of every pair to learn which tests fail. Its oracle is the run alone: a pair whose tree copy loses a failing test must not read clean; an honest twin the generator marks as provable must read clean and no honest twin reads as a finding. The oracle owes nothing to the module's tables or helpers. A dimension added to the rule and not to the generator is the reviewer's to find; a value of a dimension that no generated pair uses fails the case by name.
6. THE DOCUMENTS. The paragraph of what is not read is rewritten from the rule: what is proven, what is declined, and the short list that is still read as harmless without proof, each item with the reason it is left. The check that holds the documents' list of forms to the tables reads the list's own passage, not the whole document.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer of every earlier probe (the brief says where), except the rows of (a), (b) and (c) and the uncalled-namespace, container and partial rows, which become not compared, and the two honest rows of (c), which stop being a finding and are clean where the rule proves them and not compared where it does not - say which and why. A new bare test appended to every test file of this repository, and to every class of them that carries a decorator or a same-file base, flips nothing: both sweeps are re-run and every flip is named with the line that caused it and judged honest or not. The measurement over this repository's task commits is re-run and every changed commit judged from its diff. The payload's shape, the SET_ASIDE table's rows and the report-only use of the answer do not change. A module reached through an alias inside a helper (a store on the modules table) may move from the not-read list to not compared if the two sweeps show no flip; if they show one, it stays listed and the flip is the reason.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the guard run on real copies with both copies executed: the two inputs of (a), the six of (b), the two honest inputs of (c) as findings or not compared. The eight changes of (d) each turn a named case red. Allow twins that must stay clean: a class with a dotted skip under a single import; a bare skip with its one import; a module imported under an alias; a base from the same file that binds nothing, in any position; a namespace handed directly to an imported runner; a namespace subscripted to read. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: each rule of 1 to 4 switched off, each of the eight changes of (d), the oracle given the module's own answer in place of the run, and allow rows - a single module-level import no longer proving its name; every base declined; every namespace use declined - each turning a twin red.

NOT in this task: setattr on an object that is not the namespace; descriptors' naming hooks; a module-level attribute hook; names bound by another module at import; any language but Python; turning the report into a refusal.

Acceptance:
(1) The two inputs that lose a failing test and read clean since the last task read not compared, and so do the other inputs measured that lose one.
(2) A skip or mark spelled through a name that does not resolve is never reported as a finding, and the honest inputs under a module imported from two places are not findings.
(3) One generated case executes both copies of every pair, covers every value of every dimension the rule names, and goes red under each of the eight measured changes.
(4) A bare new test appended to every test file and every decorated or same-file-based class of this repository flips nothing, or each flip is named and judged.
(5) The README, the build guide and the changelog say what is proven, what is declined and what is left unread, true of the code.

tasks.title: The floor guard's proof is one switch per file and a short list of proven uses, a name's resolution decides only whether a reason is set aside, and the generated case holds every kind of binding and every move in every file context
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that turned the floor guard's bare-new-test reading into a proof found the proof incomplete in its own terms and two regressions in what the guard reports as a finding. Every item was run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator, both copies executed.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) A PROVEN NAME REBOUND THROUGH THE NAMESPACE. A skip name imported once, or a base bound once by a class statement, is rebound by a store through the file's namespace or through the modules-table entry; the store is seen, but it only marks the scope it stands in, so the name still resolves and a class decorated with it, or deriving from it, has its bare new test set aside: clean, a failing test lost. Two of the four measured inputs read not compared two tasks ago.
(b) REGRESSION, a finding no longer reported. With the test module imported twice, or with any star import in the file, a skip whose CONDITION is widened reads not compared where it was a finding: every argument of a call spelled like a skip is set aside when its name does not resolve, not the reason alone.
(c) REGRESSION, a finding no longer reported. Any call on a receiver named mark is taken as spelled like a mark, so a changed argument of an ordinary call inside an assertion - a dictionary or a match object named mark - reads not compared where it was a finding. This repository's own suites hold such calls.
(d) USES OF THE NAMESPACE TAKEN AS READING THAT WRITE: the namespace on the left of a membership test or in an equality with an object whose method writes into it; handed to a builtin that returns its writer or runs a metaclass hook; and two spellings not seen as the namespace at all - through the builtins module, and the dictionary of the modules-table entry. Each loses a failing test and reads clean. None of these occurs in this repository's test files.
(e) A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL: with a match capture or an except target no longer counted as a binding, the suite stays green and a name rebound that way resolves; the generated case rebinds a name by assignment only.

THE RULE TO BUILD. Smaller, not wider: the list of what is proven shrinks to what this repository's honest files need, and one switch replaces the scope-by-scope marks.
1. ONE SWITCH PER FILE. If the base copy holds, at any depth, a use of its own namespace that is not on the proven list, an exec or eval call, a star import, or a store or setattr on its own modules-table entry, then nothing in that file is proven: no name resolves, no base is followed, no bare new test is set aside, and the file reads not compared with one reason naming the first such line. The scope-by-scope reading of those forms goes.
2. THE PROVEN USES ARE A SHORT LIST, EACH SHOWN BY A RUN. The namespace - under every spelling: the names globals, locals and vars as a bare name or as the last name of an attribute, called or not, and the dictionary of the modules-table entry - is harmless only (i) handed directly, by position or keyword, to a callee that resolves to a module-level import, and (ii) in the reading forms this repository's test files really hold, found by a sweep of them and listed one by one, each with a run showing the form cannot write into it whatever the other operand is. A form no file of the repository holds is not on the list. No builtin is assumed to read.
3. RESOLUTION DECIDES ONE THING ONLY: whether the REASON argument of a skip or mark may be set aside. A call is spelled like a form only when its last name, or its last two for a mark, is a row's own name - a receiver that merely carries the name mark is not. Where the spelling matches and the name does not resolve, the reason position alone is set aside for the comparison: if anything else of the unit differs it is the finding it was before; if only the reason differs the unit reads not compared. No file context turns a changed condition, a changed assertion, a new skip or a deleted test into anything but a finding.
4. THE GENERATED CASE HOLDS THE KINDS AND THE CONTEXTS. Its rebinding dimension has one value for every kind of binding the resolution counts, taken from a list the module states once (a kind that cannot make a pair lose a test - a parameter, a declaration - is marked so with its reason, and a kind with neither a pair nor a reason fails by name). It gains the pairs of (a) and (d). And it gains a second property with its own dimensions - each move the guard reports (a widened condition, a changed assertion, a new skip, a deleted test, a changed reason) in each file context (one import; the module imported twice; a star import; a local named for a mark or a skip; a same-file function named skip) - held to: every move but the changed reason is a finding in every context, and the changed reason is clean where its name resolves and not compared where it does not.
5. THE DOCUMENTS say the switch, the short list with what was swept to make it, and what a name's resolution decides; the passage on what the reading does not claim keeps its sentence that an author set on defeating it can.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer of every earlier probe (the brief says where) except the rows above. The two sweeps - a bare new test appended to every test file, and to every decorated or same-file-based class of them - flip nothing, or each flip is named with its line and judged. The measurement over this repository's task commits is re-run, and besides the verdicts it compares the FINDINGS themselves against the tree two tasks ago: a finding reported then and not now is named and judged - the seven commits that gained a clause last time are re-read for exactly this. The payload's shape, the SET_ASIDE rows and the report-only use do not change.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, with both copies executed where a test is lost: the four inputs of (a), the widened conditions of (b) under two imports and under a star import for both test frameworks, the two changed assertions of (c), the seven inputs of (d), and the two switched-off binding kinds of (e) green over the suite. Allow twins that must stay as they are: a namespace handed directly to an imported runner; each reading form on the list; a skip imported once and used; a changed reason under one import (clean) and under two (not compared). A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the switch made scope-by-scope again; each form taken off the proven list (a twin goes red) and one unproven form put on it (a losing pair goes red); every argument set aside under an unresolved name; a receiver named mark taken as a mark; each binding kind switched off in turn; the move property's oracle given the module's own answer.

NOT in this task: a callee of another module that writes into the namespace it is handed; the text an exec or eval runs beyond turning the switch; setattr on an object that is not the modules-table entry; descriptors, attribute hooks, names bound by another module; any language but Python.

Acceptance:
(1) A name rebound through the namespace or the modules-table entry no longer resolves, and the four measured inputs read not compared.
(2) A widened skip condition and a changed assertion are findings whatever the file imports or names, and only a changed reason under an unresolved name reads not compared.
(3) The proven uses of the namespace are a list made from a sweep of this repository's test files, each with a run, and the seven measured inputs read not compared.
(4) The generated case fails by name for a binding kind with no pair, and holds every reported move in every file context.
(5) Both sweeps flip nothing or each flip is judged, no finding of the tree two tasks ago is lost over the repository's task commits, and the documents say the rule as built.

tasks.title: A call is spelled like one form and its reason position is that form's own, held for every row of the table, and an attribute merely named for the namespace does not turn the switch
tasks.description:
A narrow review of the task that gave the floor guard one switch per file and made a name's resolution decide only whether a reason is set aside found one regression and one cost outside this repository. Both were run by the reviewer and again by the orchestrator.

MEASURED on the tree as it stands.
(a) REGRESSION, a finding no longer reported. A call is matched to the table's rows by its last name and by its last two, and every row that matches is taken: a conditional expected-failure mark matches its own row, which has no reason position, and also the row of the function of the same last name, whose reason is its first argument. Under a name that does not resolve - the module imported twice, a star import, or the switch turned by anything in the file - the mark's first argument, its CONDITION, is set aside as a reason, and a widened condition reads not compared where every earlier tree reported a finding. The case that holds every move in every file context has rows for two frameworks' skip forms only.
(b) A COST OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY. Any attribute whose last name is globals, locals or vars counts as the file's namespace, so a test file that stores into a template environment's dictionary of that name turns the switch and a bare new test in it reads not compared where it read clean three tasks ago. No test file of this repository holds one.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. ONE CALL, ONE FORM. A call spelled through a dotted row name is that row and no other: the match on the most trailing names wins, and a row matched on fewer names is dropped. Where rows of equal length remain - the same last name in two frameworks - their reason positions must agree, and a pair of rows that match one spelling with different reason positions fails a case by name, so the table cannot gain such a pair unseen.
2. EVERY ROW IS HELD, NOT TWO. The case that holds the moves in every file context takes its framework rows from the table: for every row, in every spelling the row is known by, under a name that resolves and under one that does not, a change of each argument that is not the row's reason is a finding, and a change of the reason alone is clean where the name resolves and not compared where it does not. The oracle is the argument the generator changed; it does not ask the module which position is the reason - the suite states each row's reason position itself, and a row of the table the suite has no entry for fails by name.
3. THE ATTRIBUTE SPELLING IS THE BUILTINS MODULE'S. An attribute named globals, locals or vars is the file's namespace only where the object it is taken from is the builtins module - a name that resolves to an import of it, or its dunder name. Any other attribute of that name is an ordinary attribute and turns nothing.
4. THE DOCUMENTS say rule 3 where they list what turns the switch.

WHAT STAYS. Every answer of every earlier probe (the brief says where) except the rows of (a), which become findings, and the row of (b), which reads clean. The two sweeps over this repository's test files are unchanged. The measurement over this repository's task commits loses no finding and moves no verdict. The payload's shape and the SET_ASIDE rows do not change.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before: the conditional expected-failure mark with its condition widened, positionally and by its documented keyword, under two imports, a star import and a turned switch - each not compared before and a finding after; a file storing into another object's attribute named globals with a bare new test - not compared before, clean after. Allow twins: the same mark's reason changed alone (clean under one import, not compared under two); the namespace reached through the builtins module still turns the switch and loses nothing unseen. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: every matching row taken again; the shorter match winning; a row's reason position moved by one; any attribute of the name turning the switch; the builtins spelling no longer turning it.

NOT in this task: any other row of the documents' list of what is read without proof; a call spelled skip on an object of the file under an unresolved name, which reads not compared as it did before this run of fixes.

Acceptance:
(1) A widened condition of a conditional expected-failure mark is a finding in every file context.
(2) A call matches one form, and two rows matching one spelling with different reason positions fail a case by name.
(3) Every row of the table, in every spelling, is held by the generated case under a resolved and an unresolved name.
(4) An attribute named for the namespace on an ordinary object turns nothing, and the builtins module's does.
(5) Both sweeps are unchanged and no finding is lost over the repository's task commits.
